1	## Chapters
2	
3	### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains
4	
5	**Tutorial:**
6	
7	1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
8	2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
9	3. “Select Lyn.”
10	4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
11	5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
12	6. “Select attack!”
13	7. “Select Lyn.”
14	8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
15	9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
16	10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
17	11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.
18	
19	**Agent notes:**
20	
21	- No tutorial prompts appear; free play. Lyn: 16 HP, Iron sword, 2 Vulneraries. Map: Lyn starts bottom-right; one Bandit (20 HP, iron axe, 10 dmg / ~39% hit) mid-left; Batta (Brigand, 21 HP, Str5 Def3, iron axe, does 10 dmg to Lyn at 40% hit) stands on the gate top-left and NEVER moves (Batta does not leave the gate).
22	- Bandit walks toward Lyn; Lyn doubles it and killed it in one round from turn 2.
23	- **Attempt 1 LOST:** Lyn attacked Batta at 16/16 HP. He hit her in combat (16→6) and again on his enemy phase → dead. Lesson: attacking on your own phase exposes Lyn to TWO swings (his counter + his own phase) before she can heal.
24	- **Attempt 2 WON (s01, turn 10, no damage taken):** Lyn waited on her starting forest tile (turns 1-3) and let the bandit come to her; killed it on turn 4. Walked to Batta, then moved to the tile directly south of the gate and chose **Wait** (not Attack): only one swing per turn, Lyn counters x2 for 5 each. Gate heals Batta +2/turn. After two waits he was at 3 HP; then Attack killed him with the first hit. Seize the gate. Lyn hit Lv2.
25	- General lesson: the forecast's "x2" icon hides Lyn's Mt number; the in-battle HUD shows DMG. Against a stationary boss, "stand adjacent and Wait" = one enemy swing per turn, and you can step away to heal any time.
26	
27	### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate
28	
29	**Tutorial:**
30	
31	1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
32	2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
33	3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
34	4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
35	5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
36	6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
37	7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
38	   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
39	8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
40	9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
41	10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
42	11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
43	12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!
44	
45	**Agent notes:**
46	
47	- **WON attempt 1 (s02, turn 8, no deaths).** No tutorial prompts; free play. Map is exactly one screen (15x10, no scrolling). Start: Sain (0,5), Kent (0,7), Lyn (2,8). Enemies: 4 Bandits (~20 HP, Str3 Def3 Spd4-5, ~5 dmg to Kent, 7-8 to Lyn) + boss Zugu (13,1) on plain, 23 HP Str6 Def4 Spd4, iron axe; Zugu NEVER moves, only attacks adjacent units on enemy phase. The bridge bandit at (13,5) also sat still until someone came within reach.
48	- Kent's iron sword is the workhorse: 8-9 dmg, ~100% hit vs bandits, takes almost nothing. Lyn (Lv2-3) doubles everything for 7x2 = kill on anything Kent softened. Sain has ONLY an iron lance (no vulnerary): weapon-triangle loss vs axes, 66% hit / takes 9 at 78% vs Zugu — keep him out of boss fights. Kent carries a Vulnerary(3).
49	- Forests cost cavalry a lot: tiles that look reachable are often orange — check the arrow end before pressing A (A on an unreachable tile does nothing).
50	- Zugu plan that worked: Kent parked at (13,2) south of him and used a Vulnerary (counts as his action, keeps him adjacent → one enemy swing, Kent counters for 8). Next turn Kent attacked (Zugu 15→7), then Lyn attacked from (12,1) (reach it via (12,3)/(12,2); (14,1) was out of Lyn's range) and doubled him dead.
51	- Using an item gives cavalry a Canto move afterward; B does not cancel it — put the cursor back on the unit and press A → Wait.
52	
53	### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits
54	
55	**Tutorial:**
56	
57	1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
58	2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
59	3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
60	4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
61	5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
62	6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
63	7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
64	8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
65	9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!
66	
67	**Agent notes:**
68	
69	- **WON attempt 1 (s03, seized turn 10, no deaths, no house visits).** No tutorial prompts; free play. Map is one screen (15x10). Start: Lyn (0,3), Sain (1,3), Kent (1,5). Forts at (2,2),(3,2). Houses bottom-left (0,7),(1,7),(0,9) (skipped). Castle occupies x=8-14; Glass (Mercenary, 20 HP, Str5 Spd5 Def3, iron sword) on throne (11,1), never moved; a Brigand guards (11,3).
70	- Bandits: 20 HP, atk 11, hit ~77. ~5 dmg to Kent, ~9 to Lyn, ~6 to Sain (axe beats lance). One comes from (7,0) toward the forts turn 1; two from the south come up column x=6 (mountains at (6,8),(7,8) — cavalry can't cross them). The one at (13,8) never moved all chapter.
71	- **The way in:** the cracked wall at (8,3) is breakable (30 HP, shows "Wall 30"). Attack it from (7,3) — only one attacker per turn. Sain (15 atk) broke it in 2 turns. The castle's south door (11,7) is reachable only over mountains, so ignore it.
72	- After the wall broke, the guard brigand came out to (8,3) and attacked Sain. Kent at (10,3) (pillar, 25% enemy hit) + kill.
73	- Glass: Sain's iron lance did 11 at 75% hit, Glass only did 3 to him. Sain attacked from (11,2), then Glass attacked Sain on enemy phase and died to the counter. Lyn seized next turn from (9,2).
74	- Lesson: Kent tanking two bandits alone on open plain went 20→5 HP in one round (bad luck at 45%). Two bandits converging = keep the tank on a fort/forest or bring Lyn adjacent to finish.
75	- Lesson: after an enemy phase that ends with a boss kill, extra A presses can select a unit on the next player phase — screenshot before pressing more.
76	
77	### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries
78	
79	**Tutorial:**
80	
81	1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
82	2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
83	3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
84	4. Please select Lyn.
85	5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
86	6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
87	7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
88	8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
89	9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
90	10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
91	11. Select Wil.
92	12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
93	13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
94	14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
95	15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
96	16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
97	17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
98	18. You can also check on the item screen.
99	19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
100	20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
101	21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
102	22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.
103	
104	**Agent notes:**
105	
106	- **WON attempt 1 (s04, turn 10, no deaths).** No tutorial prompts; free play. Map is one screen (15x10). Objective: Defeat all enemies (9). Start: Lyn (1,8), Florina (2,7), Sain (4,8), Kent (2,9). Lyn has 2 Vulneraries + Mani Katti (unequipped at start — equip it, Atk 12, Crit 25). Kent: iron sword, iron lance, 1 Vulnerary.
107	- Villages: (2,2) top-left = 2000 gold (Florina flew there turn 1; the sword bandit at (5,4) heads for it otherwise). (3,6) = Wil (Lyn visits turn 1; Wil appears at (3,7)). Armory at (13,7) sells only iron sword/lance — skipped. After a visit, flyers/cavalry get Canto.
108	- Enemies mostly sit still until someone enters their range. Archers: 18 HP, Str1 Spd3 — Kent doubles for 10x2 and kills; do 2 dmg to cavalry/Wil, but ~19 effective to Florina, so keep her far from them.
109	- **Key choke:** forest at (10,6). Walls: row 5 (x5-10), column x=7 (rows 3-7), fence column x=10 (rows 7-9). A unit on (10,6) plugs the only passage from the east/north into the SW area, so only ONE enemy can melee it (from (11,6)). Kent sat there (forest +20 avoid) and killed brigand, swordsman and mercenary on counters while Wil (range 2 from (9,6)/(9,7)) softened them.
110	- Boss Migal (Brigand, 25 HP, Str7 Def5, steel axe Atk 18, AS 2) at (13,0) on plain, NEVER moved even with Wil in his displayed range. Wil from (13,2) (ruins) does 7, no counter: two turns of chip -> 11 HP, then Kent from (12,0) (road) doubled him (9x2, 100% hit) for the kill. (13,2) not reachable from (11,5) in one Wil move — stage at (12,2) the turn before.
111	- Interface lessons: after closing an R-screen/range display with B, the next few cursor presses can be dropped — screenshot to find the cursor before pressing A. A pressed on an empty tile opens the map menu (Unit/Status/Options/Suspend/End) — never press A blindly near Suspend.
112	
113	### Chapter 4 — In Occupation's Shadow
114	
115	**Tutorial:**
116	
117	1. “In this chapter, your goal is to protect a special character for a set period of time. Keep Natalie safe for 7 turns. Natalie, and other green units are called NPCs. NPCs are not enemies, but they cannot be moved or given orders. Sometimes, green units will be attacked because they are on the field of combat. Be careful not to let enemies close in on Natalie.”
118	2. “When the enemy far outnumbers your group, it’s safer to restrict the battle to smaller areas. No matter how strong an enemy is, if he’s attacked on all sides, he’s sure to take massive damage. So, the east door is Lyn’s, and the south door is everyone else’s. Be on guard. Select Lyn, move her to the space indicated by the cursor, and have her wait.”
119	3. “Sometimes, you can speak with enemy characters. If you think you can converse with someone, move one of your units to an adjacent space. By and large, you’ll know whom to send from hints you receive in other conversations. When you’re not sure, just try using Lyn. Select Lyn now.”
120	4. “In this way, you can sometimes turn enemies into allies. Never underestimate the power of persuasive speech. Your new companion, Dorcas, is an axe-wielding fighter. Do you remember the weapon triangle? Axes are strong against lances and weak against swords. Axes have more power than other weapons, but they are also more difficult to hit with. Try using Dorcas to attack. Select Dorcas now.”
121	5. “The weapon Dorcas is wielding is called a handaxe. Use it to attack an adjacent opponent, or throw it in indirect combat in the manner of a bow. This versatility makes it a valuable weapon. It’s difficult to hit with, though, so don’t rely on it too much. Now let’s use the handaxe and try some indirect combat.”
122	6. “Right now, after all of your units have moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn, right? Sometimes, there are moments when you might not want or be able to move all your units. When it’s bothersome to tell your units to wait one by one, select end from the map menu to speed things up. To display the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button.”
123	
124	**Agent notes:**
125	
126	- **WON attempt 1 (s05, survived 7 turns, no deaths, Dorcas recruited).** No tutorial prompts. The win triggers during enemy phase 7 (boss "Curses!" line, then Lyn "We've won!!!"). Map is 15 wide and ~13 tall, scrolls vertically. Natalie (NPC) sits in a small north room at (7,3); her only access is the 1-tile corridor (7,4) into the main room.
127	- Exits from the main room: **east door** at (11,5) (1 tile; outside is (12,5)) and **south door**, a 2-wide corridor at x=5,6 rows 8-9 (outside starts row 10). Also a **breakable wall** at (3,4) on the west (50 HP) — enemies (a fighter + mercenary) DID break it on enemy phase 6 and walked in on turn 7. Plan for it: someone inside near (5,6) / Florina on (7,4) guarding Natalie's corridor.
128	- Formation that worked: Lyn at (10,5)→(11,5) (inside the east door), Kent (iron sword, takes 3 from bandits, kills on counters) at (5,9), Sain at (6,9), Wil behind at (6,8) shooting range 2 into (6,10), Florina idle inside. Only one melee attacker reaches each door tile.
129	- Dorcas (Fighter, 30 HP, hand axe, Atk 14) starts at (13,6) and walks to (12,5) on turn 1. Turn 2: Lyn stepped onto (11,5) and Talked → recruited. With Dorcas on (12,5), Lyn on the door tile can't be meleed. Dorcas took 5/hit from the NE mercenary reinforcements (3 mercs appear around turn 4 at the NE); on turn 6 (10 HP) he retreated inside through Lyn and drank a Vulnerary; Lyn healed and Dorcas then held the door.
130	- Enemy stats: Brigands 20 HP Atk 11-12 hit 75; Mercenaries 17-18 HP Atk 8 hit 106 (5 dmg to Dorcas, 1 to Kent, ~6 to Lyn); archers 18 HP. Boss Carjiga (27 HP) + archer stay bottom-right and never came.
131	- Sain with iron lance is a poor south blocker (takes 6/hit from bandits, 67% hit) — needed both his Vulneraries. Kent's iron sword is down to ~11 uses; Kent also carries an iron lance.
132	- Interface: turned battle animations OFF, game speed Fast, text Max in Options (turn 3) — much faster. Using a Vulnerary on a cavalry unit gives Canto: put the cursor back on the unit, A → Wait.
133	
134	### Chapter 5 — Beyond the Borders
135	
136	**Tutorial:**
137	
138	1. “Sometimes, you can talk to different NPCs (the green units on the map). The process is the same as talking to enemies. Give it a try. Please select Lyn. (Lyn selected)”
139	2. Erk, a mage, and Serra, a cleric, have joined your group. Mages use the magic of truth to attack and damage their enemies. Clerics use staves to restore HP to their allies. Let’s try them both. First, select Serra.
140	3. Press the A button, and select the staff from the menu.
141	4. “Clerics cannot wield weapons; therefore they can’t engage in combat. However, they can use their staves to restore HP to allied units. Besides healing staves, which restore HP, there are other staves with different abilities. It’s always a good idea to test out any new abilities you receive, so let’s do that now. Have Erk demonstrate his magic. Begin by selecting Erk.”
142	5. “Magic, like Dorcas’s throwing axes, can strike enemies in adjacent squares as well as those at a distance. It’s very useful. Magic can penetrate even the strongest defenses, so it can be used in many situations. However, mages have few HP and low defensive abilities. To avoid counter-attacks, move in close to archers, and attack other fighters from 1 space away. Try and formulate combat strategies like this to be successful on the field of combat.”
143	
144	**Agent notes:**
145	
146	- **WON attempt 1 (s06, turn 10, no deaths).** No tutorial prompts. Map is one screen (15x10). Objective: Defeat all enemies (7). Start: Lyn (3,6) in forest, Kent/Sain top-left, Wil (1,6), Florina (2,7), Dorcas (3,8). Erk (Erk HP 10/17 at start) and Serra are green NPCs at (7,6)/(6,6): Lyn moves to (5,6) and Talks to Serra -> both join, and both can still act that turn.
147	- Enemies: archer (7,4) 11/20 HP next to Erk; mercenary (8,2) 19 HP; brigand (3,0) comes down onto Sain turn 1; brigand on a peak (11,0) walks onto whoever visits the village (8,3); archer (14,2) STATIONARY; mercenary (12,7) guards until someone is near, then steps onto village (10,7). **Boss Bug** (14,9) Brigand 29 HP, Str8 Def8 **Res0**, steel axe Atk 19, hit 73 — **NEVER moves**, even with a unit 2 tiles away (his displayed move range is misleading).
148	- Bug kill: Erk Fire (10 dmg, 90 hit) from (13,8) + Dorcas hand axe (6 dmg) from (12,9), both range 2 = no counter. 3 turns of chip, zero risk. Never put anyone adjacent (he does 10 to Kent, 16 to Dorcas, 17 to Erk).
149	- Villages: (8,3) and (10,7) are hints only (no items). (13,2) house also visitable.
150	- Terrain: forests everywhere east of x=5 — cavalry (Kent/Sain) move very little through them; check the blue range before planning. Flyers can stand on the lake (9,7) next to (10,7). Mountains row 4 split north (archer area) from south (Bug area).
151	- Serra heals ~+10 (Heal staff, range 1) and has a Vulnerary. Kent picked up a 2nd iron sword (first one ~0 uses left).
152	- **Interface lesson:** after a Heal animation the cursor jumped somewhere unexpected; my queued "Right, A, Up, A" opened the map menu and selected End -> ended turn 1 with 6 units unmoved. Always screenshot before pressing A after any animation.
153	
154	### Chapter 6 — Blood of Pride
155	
156	**Tutorial:**
157	
158	1. The goal of this chapter is to open the doors and reach the 3 triggers located inside. To open doors, you need door keys or the services of a thief.
159	2. There may be times when you are unsure how to proceed. Start by checking Status on the Map Menu. Visiting homes or villages is also a good way to get information. Who knows what hints you might find. Let’s try visiting a house. Please select Lyn.
160	3. The thief Matthew has joined your group. Thieves have picks, which they use to open doors and chests. Picks are usable by thieves alone. It’s time to open that door. Select Matthew.
161	4. The door has been opened. With that, you can also see inside the room behind the door. Within the room there’s a different-colored floor tile. Tiles that seem different in some way might be the triggers we’re looking for. Select Rath, move him to that tile, and order him to wait. Triggers can be released by having allied units wait on them.
162	5. Thieves can use their picks to open chests. Move Matthew onto the chest, and the chest command will appear. Choose this command, and the contents of the chest will become yours. Why don’t we see what we can find? Go ahead and select Matthew.
163	6. An angelic robe increases a character’s max HP by a small amount. Select the item on the item list and use it. To view more detailed information on items, press the R Button on the item list. A thief has the skill to open doors and chests, right? That ability can only be utilized if the thief has a set of picks. The number next to an item is the number of times the item can be used before the item breaks. Keep that in mind.
164	7. If you get a weapon or staff you can’t use, don’t worry. Other members of your party might be able to wield them. Items you cannot use appear in gray text. Try trading these items to others in your group. Don’t forget: you can only trade items with one other character at a time.
165	
166	**Agent notes:**
167	
168	- **WON attempt 1 (s07, turn 9, no deaths).** No tutorial prompts. Map ~18 wide x 14 tall, scrolls both ways; town on the west, castle (rooms hidden under roofs) in the middle/east. Objective "Trigger 3 switches". 7 enemies, all weak: 2 bandits + 1 mercenary in the town (killed turns 1-2), Soldiers (Str3 Spd1 Def0, 20 HP — harmless), 1 archer, boss Bool.
169	- **Matthew is NOT from a house.** He walks in by himself at the start of turn 3 and talks to Lyn (auto-joins). Don't waste Lyn's turns visiting houses for him. Houses: top-left = weapon-rank hint; red-roof village just north of the start = **Door Key** for Lyn (handy: a 2nd door opener). Matthew also starts with a Door Key + Lockpick.

## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

- No tutorial prompts appear; free play. Lyn: 16 HP, Iron sword, 2 Vulneraries. Map: Lyn starts bottom-right; one Bandit (20 HP, iron axe, 10 dmg / ~39% hit) mid-left; Batta (Brigand, 21 HP, Str5 Def3, iron axe, does 10 dmg to Lyn at 40% hit) stands on the gate top-left and NEVER moves (Batta does not leave the gate).
- Bandit walks toward Lyn; Lyn doubles it and killed it in one round from turn 2.
- **Attempt 1 LOST:** Lyn attacked Batta at 16/16 HP. He hit her in combat (16→6) and again on his enemy phase → dead. Lesson: attacking on your own phase exposes Lyn to TWO swings (his counter + his own phase) before she can heal.
- **Attempt 2 WON (s01, turn 10, no damage taken):** Lyn waited on her starting forest tile (turns 1-3) and let the bandit come to her; killed it on turn 4. Walked to Batta, then moved to the tile directly south of the gate and chose **Wait** (not Attack): only one swing per turn, Lyn counters x2 for 5 each. Gate heals Batta +2/turn. After two waits he was at 3 HP; then Attack killed him with the first hit. Seize the gate. Lyn hit Lv2.
- General lesson: the forecast's "x2" icon hides Lyn's Mt number; the in-battle HUD shows DMG. Against a stationary boss, "stand adjacent and Wait" = one enemy swing per turn, and you can step away to heal any time.

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s02, turn 8, no deaths).** No tutorial prompts; free play. Map is exactly one screen (15x10, no scrolling). Start: Sain (0,5), Kent (0,7), Lyn (2,8). Enemies: 4 Bandits (~20 HP, Str3 Def3 Spd4-5, ~5 dmg to Kent, 7-8 to Lyn) + boss Zugu (13,1) on plain, 23 HP Str6 Def4 Spd4, iron axe; Zugu NEVER moves, only attacks adjacent units on enemy phase. The bridge bandit at (13,5) also sat still until someone came within reach.
- Kent's iron sword is the workhorse: 8-9 dmg, ~100% hit vs bandits, takes almost nothing. Lyn (Lv2-3) doubles everything for 7x2 = kill on anything Kent softened. Sain has ONLY an iron lance (no vulnerary): weapon-triangle loss vs axes, 66% hit / takes 9 at 78% vs Zugu — keep him out of boss fights. Kent carries a Vulnerary(3).
- Forests cost cavalry a lot: tiles that look reachable are often orange — check the arrow end before pressing A (A on an unreachable tile does nothing).
- Zugu plan that worked: Kent parked at (13,2) south of him and used a Vulnerary (counts as his action, keeps him adjacent → one enemy swing, Kent counters for 8). Next turn Kent attacked (Zugu 15→7), then Lyn attacked from (12,1) (reach it via (12,3)/(12,2); (14,1) was out of Lyn's range) and doubled him dead.
- Using an item gives cavalry a Canto move afterward; B does not cancel it — put the cursor back on the unit and press A → Wait.

### Chapter 2 — Sword of Spirits

**Tutorial:**

1. The three buildings to the south are homes. You can speak with the people who live there. They sometimes give you combat hints or useful information about the land and the people. It pays to listen!
2. Next, send Sain to visit another home. Start by selecting Sain.
3. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Sain his orders.
4. Finally, let’s send Kent to visit the remaining home. This visit isn’t necessary for combat purposes. However, its residents may have useful knowledge. I recommend stopping by. Select Kent.
5. Now, send Kent to visit the next home. First, select Kent.
6. Remember, your mounted units possess the ability to move again. After moving, cavalry can move the rest of their movement range, unless they’ve received attack or staff commands. This also goes for units mounted on pegasi and wyverns. Now, give Kent his orders.
7. You should know something about fortresses. Fortresses offer more protection than woods do. Fighting from a space in a fortress is beneficial. Remember, this holds true for friend and foe alike. Keep this in mind before engaging your enemy. Fortresses also allow injured units to regain hit points. Your units automatically regain some HP at the beginning of your turn. The HP you recover in one turn is fairly small. As long as you remain in a fortress, you’ll regain HP every turn, so a full recovery is possible. There are other places where units can recover HP, including castle gates, thrones, and areas where bosses are found.
8. This chapter’s goal is to seize the throne. The leader of the enemy is on the throne now. Defeat him and have Lyn seize the throne to finish this battle. His name is Glass. He’s a sword-bearing mercenary. Think of the weapons triangle… What weapon is able to best a sword? Correct! The lance! Using the right weapon is like a shortcut to victory. To get into the altar, try using the method that you heard earlier. It’s up to you, Mark. Good luck.
9. Sometimes, you’ll get items after defeating enemies. A single unit can carry a maximum of five items. You might need to drop some old items to pick up new ones. Bear this in mind. You can see what items your enemies will drop by checking their inventories. Place the cursor on an enemy or ally, then press the R Button to view their personal data. This data screen contains information about the unit you’ve selected. Press the + Control Pad left and right to change pages and view items. If any of the items are glowing yellow, you will get them if you defeat the unit. Don’t forget!

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s03, seized turn 10, no deaths, no house visits).** No tutorial prompts; free play. Map is one screen (15x10). Start: Lyn (0,3), Sain (1,3), Kent (1,5). Forts at (2,2),(3,2). Houses bottom-left (0,7),(1,7),(0,9) (skipped). Castle occupies x=8-14; Glass (Mercenary, 20 HP, Str5 Spd5 Def3, iron sword) on throne (11,1), never moved; a Brigand guards (11,3).
- Bandits: 20 HP, atk 11, hit ~77. ~5 dmg to Kent, ~9 to Lyn, ~6 to Sain (axe beats lance). One comes from (7,0) toward the forts turn 1; two from the south come up column x=6 (mountains at (6,8),(7,8) — cavalry can't cross them). The one at (13,8) never moved all chapter.
- **The way in:** the cracked wall at (8,3) is breakable (30 HP, shows "Wall 30"). Attack it from (7,3) — only one attacker per turn. Sain (15 atk) broke it in 2 turns. The castle's south door (11,7) is reachable only over mountains, so ignore it.
- After the wall broke, the guard brigand came out to (8,3) and attacked Sain. Kent at (10,3) (pillar, 25% enemy hit) + kill.
- Glass: Sain's iron lance did 11 at 75% hit, Glass only did 3 to him. Sain attacked from (11,2), then Glass attacked Sain on enemy phase and died to the counter. Lyn seized next turn from (9,2).
- Lesson: Kent tanking two bandits alone on open plain went 20→5 HP in one round (bad luck at 45%). Two bandits converging = keep the tank on a fort/forest or bring Lyn adjacent to finish.
- Lesson: after an enemy phase that ends with a boss kill, extra A presses can select a unit on the next player phase — screenshot before pressing more.

### Chapter 3 — Band of Mercenaries

**Tutorial:**

1. The red-roofed buildings are villages. Villages are in danger of being attacked.
2. If an enemy unit reaches a village before one of our units does, the village will be destroyed.
3. As quickly as possible, visit the residents and give them warning. Only good can come of it. So, let’s visit them.
4. Please select Lyn.
5. By visiting a village, we gained a new companion. Wil is an archer. He uses a bow to fight.
6. Bows can be fired at foes more than 1 space away. Obstacles won’t affect your line of fire.
7. Attacking enemies without moving next to them is called indirect combat.
8. If the enemy has no weapons capable of indirect combat, there’s no fear of counterattack, and that’s to our benefit.
9. However, you cannot fire on adjacent spaces. If someone moves next to you and attacks, that’s it.
10. Units with bows are best suited to lend assistance from the rear. Let’s try some indirect combat, shall we?
11. Select Wil.
12. Next is Florina, a pegasus knight. As you might guess, pegasus knights have the ability to fly. They can move over almost any terrain type. This small wall would stop most units, but it poses no problem for a pegasus knight. Select Florina.
13. Knowing your units and their abilities and knowing how to use them in battle is a shortcut to victory.
14. To learn everything about a unit, place the cursor on that unit and press the R Button.
15. Weapons have the strength to be used only a limited number of times. As you fight, their endurance drops.
16. At zero, the weapon breaks and disappears from your inventory.
17. Check your weapon endurance by placing the cursor on a unit and pressing the R Button.
18. You can also check on the item screen.
19. The number next to the weapon is its endurance. Be careful. Without a weapon a unit cannot enter combat.
20. Units that fly, like pegasus knights, are very vulnerable to bow attacks.
21. Arrows will deal critical damage to them.
22. If the enemy has bow-wielding units, you must be extremely cautious.

**Agent notes:**

Lyn has 2 Vulneraries + Mani Katti (unequipped at start — equip it, Atk 12, Crit 25). Kent: iron sword, iron lance, 1 Vulnerary.

- **Key choke:** forest at (10,6). Walls: row 5 (x5-10), column x=7 (rows 3-7), fence column x=10 (rows 7-9). A unit on (10,6) plugs the only passage from the east/north into the SW area, so only ONE enemy can melee it (from (11,6)). Kent sat there (forest +20 avoid) and killed brigand, swordsman and mercenary on counters while Wil (range 2 from (9,6)/(9,7)) softened them.

Wil from (13,2) (ruins) does 7, no counter: two turns of chip -> 11 HP, then Kent from (12,0) (road) doubled him (9x2, 100% hit) for the kill. (13,2) not reachable from (11,5) in one Wil move — stage at (12,2) the turn before.

### Chapter 4 — In Occupation's Shadow

**Tutorial:**

1. “In this chapter, your goal is to protect a special character for a set period of time. Keep Natalie safe for 7 turns. Natalie, and other green units are called NPCs. NPCs are not enemies, but they cannot be moved or given orders. Sometimes, green units will be attacked because they are on the field of combat. Be careful not to let enemies close in on Natalie.”
2. “When the enemy far outnumbers your group, it’s safer to restrict the battle to smaller areas. No matter how strong an enemy is, if he’s attacked on all sides, he’s sure to take massive damage. So, the east door is Lyn’s, and the south door is everyone else’s. Be on guard. Select Lyn, move her to the space indicated by the cursor, and have her wait.”
3. “Sometimes, you can speak with enemy characters. If you think you can converse with someone, move one of your units to an adjacent space. By and large, you’ll know whom to send from hints you receive in other conversations. When you’re not sure, just try using Lyn. Select Lyn now.”
4. “In this way, you can sometimes turn enemies into allies. Never underestimate the power of persuasive speech. Your new companion, Dorcas, is an axe-wielding fighter. Do you remember the weapon triangle? Axes are strong against lances and weak against swords. Axes have more power than other weapons, but they are also more difficult to hit with. Try using Dorcas to attack. Select Dorcas now.”
5. “The weapon Dorcas is wielding is called a handaxe. Use it to attack an adjacent opponent, or throw it in indirect combat in the manner of a bow. This versatility makes it a valuable weapon. It’s difficult to hit with, though, so don’t rely on it too much. Now let’s use the handaxe and try some indirect combat.”
6. “Right now, after all of your units have moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn, right? Sometimes, there are moments when you might not want or be able to move all your units. When it’s bothersome to tell your units to wait one by one, select end from the map menu to speed things up. To display the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button.”

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s05, survived 7 turns, no deaths, Dorcas recruited).** No tutorial prompts. The win triggers during enemy phase 7 (boss "Curses!" line, then Lyn "We've won!!!"). Map is 15 wide and ~13 tall, scrolls vertically. Natalie (NPC) sits in a small north room at (7,3); her only access is the 1-tile corridor (7,4) into the main room.
- Exits from the main room: **east door** at (11,5) (1 tile; outside is (12,5)) and **south door**, a 2-wide corridor at x=5,6 rows 8-9 (outside starts row 10). Also a **breakable wall** at (3,4) on the west (50 HP) — enemies (a fighter + mercenary) DID break it on enemy phase 6 and walked in on turn 7. Plan for it: someone inside near (5,6) / Florina on (7,4) guarding Natalie's corridor.
- Formation that worked: Lyn at (10,5)→(11,5) (inside the east door), Kent (iron sword, takes 3 from bandits, kills on counters) at (5,9), Sain at (6,9), Wil behind at (6,8) shooting range 2 into (6,10), Florina idle inside. Only one melee attacker reaches each door tile.
- Dorcas (Fighter, 30 HP, hand axe, Atk 14) starts at (13,6) and walks to (12,5) on turn 1. Turn 2: Lyn stepped onto (11,5) and Talked → recruited. With Dorcas on (12,5), Lyn on the door tile can't be meleed. Dorcas took 5/hit from the NE mercenary reinforcements (3 mercs appear around turn 4 at the NE); on turn 6 (10 HP) he retreated inside through Lyn and drank a Vulnerary; Lyn healed and Dorcas then held the door.
- Enemy stats: Brigands 20 HP Atk 11-12 hit 75; Mercenaries 17-18 HP Atk 8 hit 106 (5 dmg to Dorcas, 1 to Kent, ~6 to Lyn); archers 18 HP. Boss Carjiga (27 HP) + archer stay bottom-right and never came.
- Sain with iron lance is a poor south blocker (takes 6/hit from bandits, 67% hit) — needed both his Vulneraries. Kent's iron sword is down to ~11 uses; Kent also carries an iron lance.
- Interface: turned battle animations OFF, game speed Fast, text Max in Options (turn 3) — much faster. Using a Vulnerary on a cavalry unit gives Canto: put the cursor back on the unit, A → Wait.

### Chapter 5 — Beyond the Borders

**Tutorial:**

1. “Sometimes, you can talk to different NPCs (the green units on the map). The process is the same as talking to enemies. Give it a try. Please select Lyn. (Lyn selected)”
2. Erk, a mage, and Serra, a cleric, have joined your group. Mages use the magic of truth to attack and damage their enemies. Clerics use staves to restore HP to their allies. Let’s try them both. First, select Serra.
3. Press the A button, and select the staff from the menu.
4. “Clerics cannot wield weapons; therefore they can’t engage in combat. However, they can use their staves to restore HP to allied units. Besides healing staves, which restore HP, there are other staves with different abilities. It’s always a good idea to test out any new abilities you receive, so let’s do that now. Have Erk demonstrate his magic. Begin by selecting Erk.”
5. “Magic, like Dorcas’s throwing axes, can strike enemies in adjacent squares as well as those at a distance. It’s very useful. Magic can penetrate even the strongest defenses, so it can be used in many situations. However, mages have few HP and low defensive abilities. To avoid counter-attacks, move in close to archers, and attack other fighters from 1 space away. Try and formulate combat strategies like this to be successful on the field of combat.”

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s06, turn 10, no deaths).** No tutorial prompts. Map is one screen (15x10). Objective: Defeat all enemies (7). Start: Lyn (3,6) in forest, Kent/Sain top-left, Wil (1,6), Florina (2,7), Dorcas (3,8). Erk (Erk HP 10/17 at start) and Serra are green NPCs at (7,6)/(6,6): Lyn moves to (5,6) and Talks to Serra -> both join, and both can still act that turn.
- Enemies: archer (7,4) 11/20 HP next to Erk; mercenary (8,2) 19 HP; brigand (3,0) comes down onto Sain turn 1; brigand on a peak (11,0) walks onto whoever visits the village (8,3); archer (14,2) STATIONARY; mercenary (12,7) guards until someone is near, then steps onto village (10,7). **Boss Bug** (14,9) Brigand 29 HP, Str8 Def8 **Res0**, steel axe Atk 19, hit 73 — **NEVER moves**, even with a unit 2 tiles away (his displayed move range is misleading).
- Bug kill: Erk Fire (10 dmg, 90 hit) from (13,8) + Dorcas hand axe (6 dmg) from (12,9), both range 2 = no counter. 3 turns of chip, zero risk. Never put anyone adjacent (he does 10 to Kent, 16 to Dorcas, 17 to Erk).
- Villages: (8,3) and (10,7) are hints only (no items). (13,2) house also visitable.
- Terrain: forests everywhere east of x=5 — cavalry (Kent/Sain) move very little through them; check the blue range before planning. Flyers can stand on the lake (9,7) next to (10,7). Mountains row 4 split north (archer area) from south (Bug area).
- Serra heals ~+10 (Heal staff, range 1) and has a Vulnerary. Kent picked up a 2nd iron sword (first one ~0 uses left).
- **Interface lesson:** after a Heal animation the cursor jumped somewhere unexpected; my queued "Right, A, Up, A" opened the map menu and selected End -> ended turn 1 with 6 units unmoved. Always screenshot before pressing A after any animation.

### Chapter 6 — Blood of Pride

**Tutorial:**

1. The goal of this chapter is to open the doors and reach the 3 triggers located inside. To open doors, you need door keys or the services of a thief.
2. There may be times when you are unsure how to proceed. Start by checking Status on the Map Menu. Visiting homes or villages is also a good way to get information. Who knows what hints you might find. Let’s try visiting a house. Please select Lyn.
3. The thief Matthew has joined your group. Thieves have picks, which they use to open doors and chests. Picks are usable by thieves alone. It’s time to open that door. Select Matthew.
4. The door has been opened. With that, you can also see inside the room behind the door. Within the room there’s a different-colored floor tile. Tiles that seem different in some way might be the triggers we’re looking for. Select Rath, move him to that tile, and order him to wait. Triggers can be released by having allied units wait on them.
5. Thieves can use their picks to open chests. Move Matthew onto the chest, and the chest command will appear. Choose this command, and the contents of the chest will become yours. Why don’t we see what we can find? Go ahead and select Matthew.
6. An angelic robe increases a character’s max HP by a small amount. Select the item on the item list and use it. To view more detailed information on items, press the R Button on the item list. A thief has the skill to open doors and chests, right? That ability can only be utilized if the thief has a set of picks. The number next to an item is the number of times the item can be used before the item breaks. Keep that in mind.
7. If you get a weapon or staff you can’t use, don’t worry. Other members of your party might be able to wield them. Items you cannot use appear in gray text. Try trading these items to others in your group. Don’t forget: you can only trade items with one other character at a time.

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s07, turn 9, no deaths).** No tutorial prompts. Map ~18 wide x 14 tall, scrolls both ways; town on the west, castle (rooms hidden under roofs) in the middle/east. Objective "Trigger 3 switches". 7 enemies, all weak: 2 bandits + 1 mercenary in the town (killed turns 1-2), Soldiers (Str3 Spd1 Def0, 20 HP — harmless), 1 archer, boss Bool.
- **Matthew is NOT from a house.** He walks in by himself at the start of turn 3 and talks to Lyn (auto-joins). Don't waste Lyn's turns visiting houses for him. Houses: top-left = weapon-rank hint; red-roof village just north of the start = **Door Key** for Lyn (handy: a 2nd door opener). Matthew also starts with a Door Key + Lockpick.
- **Switch 1:** door directly north of the start area (the barred gate in the wall above the red-roof village). Matthew opens it turn 3, Rath steps on the blue tile inside. This removes the hall roof and opens the hall to the town on its west side.
- **Switch 2:** the east door (south side of the castle, guarded by a Soldier outside; kill it first). Room inside has a Soldier standing ON the switch — he attacked Sain and died on the counter, then Sain stepped on it. I opened this door with the village Door Key passed Lyn -> Erk -> Sain (trading is free, chain it).
- **Switch 3:** under **boss Bool** (Knight, 26 HP, Str8 Def10 **Res0**, steel lance Atk18, never moves) in the room north of the hall, revealed by switch 2 along with an archer (20 HP, weak). Erk Fire did 10x2 from 2 tiles away (no counter), Kent's iron lance finished (6x2, 92%). Then Matthew waited on Bool's tile -> win.
- Chests: hall chest = Angelic Robe (Matthew still holds it — give to Lyn), small room north of the hall (door the hall soldier guarded) = **Armorslayer** (Matthew holds it; forecast vs Bool showed only 8 dmg / 69% hit, so it is not as strong as hoped).
- Interface: after a kill the EXP bar shows; DON'T press A to dismiss — it falls through and opens the map menu / Unit screen. Use B or just wait. Mounted units get Canto after opening a door with a key.

### Chapter 7 — Siblings Abroad

**Tutorial:**

1. Starting with this chapter, you’ll be able to use the preparations screen. On this screen, you can choose who will fight, equip different items, and arrange your formation, among other things. If you have no special preparations to make, simply press START. This starts the chapter with the same group you were using at the end of the last chapter.
2. The monk Lucius has joined your group. Monks are users of the magic of light. Those who wield magic are highly attuned to its flow, so they have a high magic resistance. Units with high magic resistances can reduce the damage caused by magical attacks. When magic users battle each other, they often find it hard to inflict damage. The light magic of monks is strong against the dark magic favored by shamans. Lucius should come in handy here. Let’s put his magic to the test. Have Lucius attack the shaman nearest him.
3. It’s time to see what Nils can do. The music played by bards allows your allies to move twice in the same turn. However, bards cannot engage in combat, so be careful not to expose them to danger.
4. Through the power of Nils’s music, Lucius can move again this turn. Bards gain experience by playing music. Use Nils’s powers often, and increase his skill.
5. When you fulfill certain conditions, side quests may make themselves apparent to you. Side quests allow you to learn things that aren’t part of the main story. You might meet tough new enemies or find new companions to travel with. However, side quests are very difficult, and once you begin one, you must see it through to its end. If you plan to challenge a side quest, I suggest you keep the save data from the previous mission. Not accepting side quests will not effect your ranking. If you’re in a hurry to pursue the main story, skip the side quests.

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s08, Heintz killed turn 11, no deaths).** Details below.
- Terrain gotchas: the tile just SOUTH of the (13,5) bridge is a **mountain** (infantry crawl, cavalry can't pass), so Kent/Sain/Rath never got past the bridge; only Lyn, Dorcas, Lucius did the final push. Next time send the infantry/magic units toward the bridge early and use the cavalry for the north fights only.
- Heintz did NOT move off his gate. He attacks anyone within Flux range 2 and the gate heals him (+2-ish per turn). Lucius (light) did 7 per hit to him at 86%, Lyn (Mani Katti) 7x2 at 68%. Kill tile that worked for Lyn: directly SOUTH of Heintz (the tile east of him was not reachable). Two shamans + 1 mage guard the castle side; each walks one step toward you per turn and does ~8 to Dorcas; Dorcas (iron axe) doubles shamans for 10-11 each.
- Ending: "Embark on side quest?" prompt -> chose **Yes** (highlighted default) -> Chapter 7x. Saved to slot 1.
- (s08, attempt 1, notes taken mid-play) Fielded Lyn, Sain, Kent, Wil, Dorcas, Erk, Serra, Rath (Florina benched; Matthew's Angelic Robe -> Lyn via Prep Trade, Lyn 24 HP). Nils + Lucius are extra player units at the start. Map ~20x14, scrolls. Start top-left. Village at (7,2) is a **general store** (Vulnerary/Heal/Fire). Heintz (Shaman, 22 HP, Mag3 Spd7 Def3 Res5) sits on a gate at about (7,10), south of a castle; peaks/mountains wall the castle off from the north and a river cuts off the west, so the route is EAST: road east to (13,4), bridge (13,5) south, then west over the bridge by the fort at (10,9)/(11,9). Enemies came to us turns 1-6 (archer, 2 fighters, merc, mage, shaman) — Rath (bow, 10x2) and Kent (iron sword) killed most; bait with Lyn/Dorcas at the bridge worked.
- (s07 handover, before play) The game was left on the **Preparations** screen (Pick Units / Trade / Fortune / Check Map / Save; START = Fight). Objective shown: **Defeat Heintz**. In the opening cutscene the party starts top-left of the map, Nils is a green NPC beside them, and a shaman + an archer were visible a few tiles east/south-east. Consider using Prep Trade to give Matthew's **Angelic Robe** to Lyn (+HP).

### Chapter 7x — The Black Shadow (gaiden)

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s09, rout finished enemy phase 12, no deaths).** Fielded Lucius instead of Florina (Lucius MVP: 11x2 light magic, 0 dmg taken from mages, killed ~6 units). 12 enemies + 3 reinforcements (soldiers that spawn on the stairs tile inside the boss-ish room in the middle; they walk out through an opening in that room's left wall). All enemies are weak Lv1-2 generics (20 HP soldiers, 21 HP fighters, 19 HP mercs Res 0, 16 HP mage/shaman).
- The real boss is **Beyard** (steel sword, 24 HP) in the small top-left room, NOT the red mage on the middle throne (that one is a generic Lv1 mage that walks out and attacks). Beyard never moves. Sain (lance, Lv5 Def 8) did 13/hit at 91% and took 6; two rounds killed him (attack + counter on enemy phase). Route to him: west column x=7 -> north via column x=9 -> top corridor west to x=5 -> down to row 4 -> up into his room through the gap at (2,3). Cavalry does it in 2 turns.
- Plan that worked: start (bottom-right) is a closed pocket with two chokes: the 1-tile gap north of the start group (Dorcas/Kent held it vs the cavalier and mage) and the 2-wide stairs on the west (Rath/Sain/Lucius). Wait 1-2 turns, kill what comes with ranged (Erk/Lucius/Rath at range 2), then push north up the west column. Two pillar mercs stay put until you are in their 5-move range; bait them with a tanky unit at the top of the column.
- Chest in the room with the archer (west side) was never opened (a hooded enemy stood on it for a turn but it stayed closed). Not needed.
- Interface: the camera scrolls a lot on this map (15 wide x ~17 tall); after every move take a fresh screenshot before trusting coordinates. On a move, if A does nothing, the tile is orange/unreachable — check where the arrow head ends.
- (s08 handover, before play) Left on the **Preparations** screen, objective **"Defeat enemy"** (rout). The opening pan showed an indoor fortress/castle map: stone corridors and rooms, many enemies (soldiers/lances, fighters, a mercenary, an archer in a room with a chest bottom-left, a mage-type boss on a throne-like tile bottom-centre, a cavalier top-right). Lucius and Nils are still in the party from Ch7; Lucius was excellent vs shamans.
- Interface tips from Ch7 (they apply here too): during a move, if A does nothing the tile is unreachable (look at where the blue arrow's head actually ends). Fort/forest/mountain costs make infantry ranges much smaller than they look. After a kill, press B (not A) to clear the EXP bar.

### Chapter 8 — Vortex of Strategy

**Tutorial:**

1. On the far side of the hill to the south is a ballista. As Kent said, it’s a weapon intended for trained archers. The attack range of ballistae is extremely large, so they can fire on enemies at great distance. As they can attack without fear of counterattack, they’re quite useful. To use one, move an archer onto an unoccupied ballista, and select the ride command. After that, you can attack as usual. Ballistae can also be moved while in use. Additionally, ballistae can be used by any archer in the field. So, if you can remove the enemy manning the ballista and move one of your group onto it… you’ll find it most useful.

**Agent notes:**

- (s09 handover, before play) Left on the **Preparations** screen (cursor on Pick Units), objective **"Defeat enemy"**, 9/9 units. Current pick list showed Lyn, Sain, Kent, Wil, Dorcas, Erk, Serra, Rath, Lucius fielded; Matthew, Florina, Nils benched (game's default — I did not change it). Opening cutscene: party starts top-left on grass; a village/town top-right; an enemy **ballista** (archer on it) sits in the mountains south-centre and shot Lyn in the cutscene (Lyn showed 24 HP). Per tutorial: kill the ballista's archer and put Wil/Rath on it.
- **WON attempt 1 (s10 played turns 1-3, s13 finished turn 14; no deaths).** Kent (Lv8, iron lance + iron sword + Vulnerary) did most of the work; Sain helped. The rest of the army never got off the start plateau area in time — the cliffs/mountains make the middle of the map slow; next time send infantry down the WEST column (x=0-3) early.
- The SE reaver group + Yogi do NOT move until you get close; then they come at the closest unit. Kent at (10,14) with the iron sword equipped baited the Lancereaver merc + Swordreaver brigand; Sain's lance killed the brigand. Yogi (Def high) took 6x2 from Kent's sword (100% hit, Yogi 30% hit/9 dmg); two rounds + one counter-round killed him. The ballista at (9,8) is walled in by mountains — Wil could NOT reach it.
- Interface: after using a Vulnerary, a cavalier gets Canto (a small blue move range); put the cursor on his own tile and press A, then Wait.
- Game saved to slot 1 after Ch7x ("Ch. 8: Vortex of Strategy").
- (s13, attempt 1 continued from turn 4 — s10 left it there, no notes) Map 15 wide x 18 tall. Start = plateau top-left ringed by cliffs (brown-line tiles are impassable); exits south at (2,5)/(2,6)/(3,6). 13 enemies at turn 4. Enemies only trickle toward you; most are stationary until you get near. Wins so far: Kent iron LANCE does 16-17 x2 at 99% to the 20-21 HP soldiers (kills); Erk Fire 10x2 to soldiers (Res 0). The ballista archer at (9,8) never fired at us; it later got off and walked to us (Sain killed it). The brigand razed the NE village turn 5 — not worth chasing.
- **SE group (boss area, east of the (7-8,14) bridge, near fort (13,16)) uses REAVER weapons (reverse triangle):** Merc w/ Lancereaver (11,16, 18 HP — don't send Kent/Sain, use Dorcas/magic), Soldier w/ Axereaver (11,14 — not Dorcas; swords/magic), Brigand w/ Swordreaver (13,14 — not Lyn; use Kent/Sain lances), **boss Yogi** Knight Lv6 25 HP Axereaver Atk 19 at (12,15) — use Erk/Lucius magic. Plus a 4 HP merc (iron sword) and a shaman far NE (13,4).

### Chapter 9 — A Grim Reunion

**Tutorial:**

1. Wallace is a level 12 knight. He can rise as high as level 20. Most units can change classes once they reach level 10. By changing classes, units can improve all of their abilities. Movement range, constitution, usable weapons… Everything. There are many benefits. With a single action, you can make your units significantly more powerful. In order to change classes, units need to be of a certain level. However, you also need a special item. For example, Wallace is carrying a knight crest. With this, cavaliers and knights can change classes. Each character class has its own unique item that allows units of that class to switch to a different class. Well then, why don’t we try changing class now? Select Wallace, then choose knight crest from his items and use it.

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s14, seized turn 12, no deaths).** Kent (lance, then SWORD once Eagler swapped to his Hand axe) did all the boss damage: turn 10 he attacked from the tile directly below the gate (7x2, 67%), Eagler's enemy-phase attack on him let Kent counter again (30 -> 7 HP by turn 11, gate heals ~3/turn), turn 11 Kent's iron sword (6x2, 92%) killed him. Eagler hits mages for 15 and Dorcas for 11 — do NOT let fragile units sit in his range 2 (counter + enemy phase can kill them). Keep only the tank adjacent; everyone else 3+ tiles away.
- The gate (castle bottom-center) is entered only from the tile below it. Lyn is SLOW to get there: start moving her east by turn 3-4, the map is ~15 tiles of walking from the start. Seize happened turn 12 only because Lyn lagged.
- (s14, attempt 1, notes mid-play turn 7) Map 20 wide x ~15 tall, start far west. Fog rolls in at the start of turn 3 (event). Turn 1: Wallace (green->joins automatically, Lv12 Knight) used his Knight Crest -> General (34 HP, Def 17, iron lance + iron axe); nothing hurts him. Village top-left (Sain visited) = Torch. The single bridge in the middle (river) is a good choke; Kent on the bridge killed the fighter on the counter turn 1.
- Enemies are all weak Lv1-3 generics (soldiers 21 HP Def 0, brigands 20 HP, cavaliers 20 HP, archers 18 HP) but they keep trickling in from the north and east; 3 brigands sit on PEAKS in the far SW (40 avoid) and stab at whoever is near (Wallace tanks them for 0).
- Boss **Eagler** (Paladin, 30 HP, Str10 Skl6 Spd7 Def10 Res5, Javelin + Hand axe, range 1-2) stands on the castle gate in the far SE (bottom-center of the castle). Two Lv3 soldiers stand just below the gate. Plan: Wallace (takes 0) + Kent lance + magic.
- Interface: Rescue works (Sain Aid 16 carried Lyn, Con 5; Wallace Con 15 also fits), cavalry gets Canto after Rescue/Drop, but a DROPPED unit is greyed out and cannot act that turn. Eagler never left the gate through turn 9.
- (s13 handover, before play) Left on the **Preparations** screen (cursor on Pick Units), objective **"Seize gate"**. Saved to slot 1 after Ch8. Team state at end of Ch8: Kent Lv8 (strongest, carries iron sword + 2 iron lances + Vulnerary), Sain ~Lv6, Lyn Lv6, Erk Lv3, Serra Lv2; nobody dead. The opening cutscene showed Eliwood talking with Lyn in Caelin town (I skipped the dialogue with Start).

Serra's Heal staff has only 2 uses left at t4 (she has 2 Vulneraries). ### Chapter 10 — The Distant Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Here ends Lyn’s story. Would you like to save your progress? [Yes] [No]  
   Would you like to continue playing? [Yes] [No]
2. As of Chapter 11, Eliwood becomes the story’s main character. Mark’s role will be to act as tactician, aiding his group. Help Eliwood to fulfill the chapter goals and fight his way to the end of the game. You’ll start your first campaign with Eliwood, then meet his friend, Hector, in chapter 12. And who knows? You might even meet Lyn again. If any of these three is defeated, your game will be over. The game will continue if any other allied units are defeated. However, a defeated unit can never take part in combat again, so be careful!

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s15, seized turn 22, no deaths).** Boss kill: Wallace (iron AXE equipped, 77% hit, 8 dmg) stood on the tile below the gate; Lundgren swaps between Javelin (0 dmg to Wallace) and Silver lance (8 dmg, 53%). Wallace hit him t18 and t19, Lucius (light magic, 5x2 at 76%, no counter) from 2 tiles RIGHT of the gate (same row as the gate) finished him to 4 HP, and Lundgren died attacking on enemy phase 19. Kent's Armorslayer forecast was only 1 dmg x2 at 52% (Lundgren Def is high + gate bonus) — the Armorslayer plan does NOT work here. Gate is entered only from the tile directly below it; the tile right of that one (below-right of the castle) is open plain. Florina ferried Lyn (Rescue -> fly -> Drop below the gate) because Lyn is slow in the forest; "Give" (hand a carried unit to an adjacent ally) does not end the flier's turn, so she can Give then Rescue someone else.
- (s15, attempt 1, notes mid-play turn 11) Map ~18 wide x 17 tall. Start pocket top-left is closed by rivers; ONLY exit is the bridge just east of the start (~(7,2)). Route: east along the north strip -> bridge going SOUTH at the NE (~(16,6)) -> SE region -> one of two bridges WEST over the vertical river (~(11,7) and ~(11,11)) -> forest middle -> forts -> castle bottom-left. Boss **Lundgren** (General Lv5, 35 HP, Str12 Skl8 Spd5 Def14 Res7, Silver lance Atk 26 + Javelin 1-2) stands ON the gate (castle bottom-left, gate ~ (2,15)); a Lv? soldier stands below him.
- **RAIN events**: turn 2-4 and turn 8-9 it rains -> every unit's move drops to ~2-3 tiles. Plan for it (don't count on reaching anything those turns).
- Enemy waves: NE strip (soldier, mage, 2 archers) came to the bridge t2-6; SE region (shaman Flux, brigand, 3 cavaliers Lv1 iron lance 20 HP, merc) came to us t7-11. **Wallace (General, Def 17) takes 0 from all of them** — park him in front and let them suicide on his counters. A brigand razed the walled village (SE, ~(14-16,10-12)) — now "Ruins".
- Village (NE, ~(16,2)): hint only — "Lundgren destroyed the bridge; knock over a **Snag** (dead tree, 20 HP, attack it) to cross"; "visit my father's armory for weapons vs Lundgren". Snags seen at ~(16,15) and ~(7,16) along the bottom river.
- Gave Matthew's **Armorslayer to Kent** turn 1 (Kent Str ~12: Armorslayer should do ~20 x2 vs Lundgren = kill). Sain's lance broke t11; Kent gave him an iron lance.
- (s14 handover, before play) Left on the **Preparations** screen (cursor on Pick Units), objective **"Seize gate"**. Saved to slot 1 after Ch9 (slot shows "Ch. 9: A Grim Reunion"). Team after Ch9: Kent Lv10 (best unit; iron sword + 2 iron lances), **Wallace is a General** (34 HP, Def 17 — physical enemies barely scratch him; iron lance + iron axe), Lyn Lv6+, Dorcas 20/32, Sain ~11/23 (both should be back to full HP at chapter start), nobody dead. Sain's iron lance is low on uses (~11). The opening pan showed the party top-left, a bridge just east, a river across the middle, brigands south, an archer and a soldier/cavalier east.

## Eliwood mode (what the game actually loaded after Lyn's story)

### Chapter 11 — Taking Leave

**Agent notes:**

- (s15 handover, before play) After Lyn's story the game asked only "Save your progress?" (Yes -> slot 1, now "Ch. 10: The Distant Plains") and "Continue playing?" (Yes). **No mode or difficulty choice was offered** — it went straight into Eliwood's story ("One Year Later..."), so the Hector-mode headings below do not apply to this chapter. Title card: "Ch. 11: Taking Leave". There is **no Preparations screen**: the session hands over on the map at turn 1, player phase, cursor on Eliwood (18 HP). Objective **"Seize gate"**. Opening view: Eliwood + 2 cavaliers + a few others bottom-right; ~7 axe brigands spread across the top-left/middle (one next to a burning village top-left); a fort/gate-like building top-centre-right; mountains through the middle. Nothing has been moved yet on turn 1.
- Lyn-mode units (Kent, Sain, Wallace, Lucius, etc.) are NOT in Eliwood's party at this point.
- (s20, attempt 1 continued from turn 7 — s16 played t1-7 but left no notes; s17-19 died instantly on usage limits) Party: Eliwood, Marcus, Lowen, Rebecca, Dorcas, Bartre. Boss **Batta-like bandit** stood ON the gate and was killed by s16 turn 7; enemy count 0 after that.
- **WON attempt 1 (s20, seized turn 14, no deaths).** The Gate tile is the mansion's bottom-centre DOOR; it can only be entered from the tile directly below it. Don't park another unit on that tile (Marcus was standing there and blocked it). Pressing Start during the ending skipped everything straight to Ch12's map (no save prompt was seen).
- **THE GATE is the door of the burning walled mansion on the WEST/left side of the map** (terrain name "Gate", Def 2 Avo 20), NOT the castle in the top-right. The top-right castle is a **village** ("mayor's home"? visit it): Eliwood visited it turn 9 -> **Dragonshield**. Fort in the middle-right is just a Fort. I wasted turns 8-9 walking Eliwood east to the wrong place.

## Hector mode

### Chapter 11 — Another Journey

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 12 — Birds of a Feather

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s21, rout finished turn 9, no deaths).** Hector + Oswin joined permanently (they are in the party for Ch13). Last enemies (archer + mercenary) sat on the east-edge mountains; Lowen's javelin/sword finished them (Marcus can't climb the mountain tiles). After the win a **Save screen** appeared (chose slot 1, the one in use -> Save), then the world map and the Ch13 title card. Bought 1 Vulnerary (Eliwood) at the general store beside the start; Eliwood used the Dragonshield (+Def). Dorcas still carries an unused **Energy ring**.
- (s21, attempt 1, notes mid-play turn 7) Map 17 wide x 16 tall, scrolls; Start opens a minimap (red/blue dots) — the quickest way to find everyone. Enemies are weak Lv1 generics (soldier Str3 Def0 20 HP, bandits 20-22 HP iron axe). **Marcus on the fort just NE of the start (~3 tiles east of the start group) one-shots bandits on the counter**; he killed ~6 by himself. Boss **Zagan** (Fighter Lv9, 32 HP, Str11 Spd6 Def6, steel axe Atk 22) walks in from the far east edge around turn 6-7 and attacks Marcus; Marcus's counter (steel sword, 18 x2) killed him in one round, Marcus took ~0-12. **Hector (Lord, 19 HP, Def 8, Wolf Beil) + Oswin (Knight, javelin)** appear in the NORTH-WEST on turn 4 (Hector is a lord: game over if he dies) next to ~5 soldiers/archer/bandit; Hector on the village tile at the top (~(7,4), visit = just talk) took ~2 per hit and leveled. The **west column is a dead end**: the walled village top-left (visit with Eliwood from its bottom gate -> a stat book "improves fighting prowess") blocks the way north, so the start group can only go EAST. An archer sits in a cliff pocket next to the fort SW of Hector's village — only reachable at range 2 (Oswin javelin).
- (s20 handover, before play) This is still **Eliwood's story** (the game never offered a Hector/Eliwood choice), but this heading is the one used for Ch12. Game left on the **map at turn 1, player phase, nothing moved** (no Preparations screen). Objective **"Defeat all enemy units"** — 20 enemies. Party of 6: Eliwood (18/18, Lv1), Marcus, Lowen, Rebecca, Dorcas, Bartre; start group bottom-left beside two villages. Enemies seen: brigands/fighters (axes) to the north and east, a red-armoured unit top-centre near a fort, a castle/village top-left. Eliwood is holding a **Dragonshield** (from the Ch11 village) — consider using it on Eliwood or giving it to a frontliner.

### Chapter 13 — In Search of Truth

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s22, seized turn 15, no deaths).** Route: down the EAST edge (x=16-17) t1-2, kill the east-side brigands/archers t2-6 around the walled village and the fort at ~(13,13), then hold the 2-tile bridge (~(10,14)/(10,15)) with Marcus ON the bridge t7-8 — the west-bank group (fighters, archer, soldiers, merc) walked into him and died on counters/our turn. Crossed t9-10, then the 2 soldiers guarding the gate (Str 4, Def 0 — harmless) attacked Marcus and died. **Boss Boies** (Knight Lv13, 27 HP, Def 13 + gate, steel lance Atk 22, range 1 ONLY, never moves): Marcus with the **steel LANCE** (NOT the sword — lance beats sword, the sword forecast was ~0 dmg) did 11 per hit at 77%, x2; one round on t13 + his counter on enemy phase killed him. Eliwood seized t15 (the gate is the castle's bottom-centre tile; it is entered only from the tile directly below — move whoever stands there out first).
- Guy (myrmidon) appeared with a "best swordsman in Sacae" line around turn 6-7 but I never found him on the map; not recruited.
- A lone brigand wandered over from the north-west late (t12-14) and attacked the units I had left behind at the start (Rebecca dropped to 7 HP). Don't leave weak units unescorted at the start area.
- Interface: in the battle forecast the red "x2" badge can HIDE the second digit of Mt ("1x2" was really 11x2). Eliwood used his **Secret Book** (+Skl) t13. Eliwood is still Lv1 (18 HP) — feed him kills when safe.
- After the seize: Start skipped the ending -> **Save screen** (slot 1, Save) -> world map (Start) -> Ch14 opening -> Start -> **Preparations** for Chapter 14. No 13x gaiden was offered.
- (s22, attempt 1, notes mid-play turn 5) Map is 18 wide x 17 tall (x0-17, y0-16). Party (10: Eliwood Lv1, Hector, Marcus, Lowen, Oswin, Dorcas, Bartre, Rebecca, Serra, Matthew) starts top-right ~(11-17, 2-5). **Gate = bottom-centre of the burning castle in the WEST, ~(2,10)**, boss (armoured, red) stands on it; soldiers/archers/fighters around the castle. A river runs north-south down the middle (x~8-10); the ONLY crossing seen is the 2-tile bridge at ~(10,14)/(10,15) bottom-centre, guarded on its west end by soldier/fighters/merc/archer. Peaks/mountains along row 7 block the start area: the only way south is the EAST EDGE (x=16-17, rows 6-9) — infantry like Eliwood get stuck behind (go east first). Walled village (11-13,7-8): enter from its bottom gap (12,9) -> **Mine** (Marcus visited t3). House at (10,6) = flavour only. Enemies on the east side: 2 brigands + 3 archers (steel/iron bow) came to us t1-3; 3 brigands walk toward the village from the SW. Marcus's steel sword has only ~6 uses — he is using the steel lance (59% vs brigands in forest). Oswin has a Javelin (range 2).

- (s21 handover, before play) Title card "Ch. 13: In Search of Truth". Saved to slot 1 after Ch12 (slot shows "Ch. 12: Birds of a Feather"). I pressed Start once on the opening cutscene; the game then showed the **map at turn 1, player phase, nothing moved, cursor on Eliwood (18/18)** — no Preparations screen appeared. Objective **"Seize gate"**. Party: Eliwood, Hector, Marcus, Lowen, Oswin, Rebecca, Dorcas, Bartre (plus a robed/staff unit seen near the top of the start group — check who). Opening view: party in the top-centre/top-right; two houses (village + shop?) top-left across a river; a walled village in the middle below the party; a castle top-left (burning towers); enemies (a fighter on the left edge, red units bottom-left/bottom-right). Use Start for the minimap to find everyone. Team strength: Marcus (Paladin, steel sword) is the killer; Hector (Wolf Beil) and Oswin (Knight) are solid tanks; Eliwood is still fragile (Lv1-2, 18 HP) — keep him back.
