### Chapter 14 — False Friends

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s23, rout finished turn 16, no deaths).** Erk recruited (Serra talks to him). Priscilla (shown in a t2 event) was never seen on the map and NOT recruited. The last 2 enemies (a Lv2 Knight 18 HP + a cavalier) sat far SOUTH near two houses below the castle — the last 3 turns were spent walking there; send a fast unit south earlier next time. Marcus (Def 11, steel lance) did most kills; his **steel sword has 1 use left and steel lance ~9** — he needs new weapons (buy/trade at the next shop). Hector's Wolf Beil ~10 uses, Oswin's javelin ~6. Ending: Start skipped the dialogue -> Save screen (slot 1, Save) -> world map -> title card "Ch. 15: Noble Lady of Caelin" -> Preparations.
- (s23, attempt 1, notes mid-play turn 5) Objective **"Defeat enemy"** = rout (22 at start, reinforcements appear: bandits from the NW village area t3, more t4). Party starts on a peninsula top-right bounded by a river: **west bridge** (top) and **south bridge**; 4 Laus soldiers on the east sand walk in t1 and die on counters (Dorcas/Hector). Enemies are weak Lv3 generics ("Laus" soldiers Atk 11, cavaliers, archer Atk 11, brigand Atk 14) — Marcus (Def 11) takes 0-1 per hit and kills them in one round with the steel lance. Battle animations are already OFF.
- **Erk** starts as a GREEN NPC on the plateau west of the west bridge, right next to an enemy cavalry group. Recruited t4: Lowen rescued him t3 (Rescue works on green units), carried him back across the bridge t4 and Dropped him, then **Serra talked to him** -> Erk joined (Thunder, Goddess Icon). **Priscilla** (event t2) is somewhere to the west — Erk can probably recruit her.
- **Rain from turn 5**: everyone's move drops to ~2-3 tiles (rain ended turn 8).
- (s23 turn 14) Reinforcements stopped ~turn 8; count went 22 -> 21 peak -> 4 by turn 14. Waves: bandits from the NW village (one razed the north village), 5 **pirates** from the SE sea (they walk on water; ~50-60% hit on sand, Atk 13) which came at the south bridge t10-12 — Oswin as a lone wall + Hector/Dorcas/Eliwood picking them off worked. **Boss Erik** (Cavalier Lv14, 28 HP, **Horseslayer** = huge damage vs Marcus/Lowen) waits by the burning castle in the SW with 3 cavaliers; he stayed put for ~12 turns, then attacked Marcus when Marcus parked ~4 tiles away on t13 — Marcus survived and his counters killed Erik. The house at the cliff edge just west of the ruined north village is flavour only.

- (s22 handover, before play) Game left on the **Preparations** screen (cursor on Pick Units; header "Chapter 14", objective **"Defeat enemy"**). Saved to slot 1 after Ch13. Opening cutscene: party top-right of a grassy map next to a **green-hooded NPC** (looked like a merchant), Eliwood talking with Hector; a castle with burning towers on the left, a walled village top-centre, a river on the right. Team after Ch13 (nobody dead): Marcus (Paladin, steel lance ~20 uses, steel sword 6 uses) is still the carry; Hector, Oswin (javelin), Dorcas and Lowen leveled; Eliwood still Lv1 (Skl +1 from Secret Book). Marcus got a **Mine** item from the Ch13 village.

### Chapter 15 — Talons Alight

**Agent notes:**

_(none yet)_

### Chapter 16 — Noble Lady of Caelin

**Agent notes:**

- (s23 handover, before play) The game's title card says **"Ch. 15: Noble Lady of Caelin"** (Eliwood-story numbering; this file's headings use Hector numbering, so this is the right section — there is no Ch15 "Talons Alight" in this route). Game left on the **Preparations** screen (cursor on Pick Units, header "Chapter 15"), objective **"Seize gate"**. Saved to slot 1 after Ch14. Party (11, nobody dead): Eliwood Lv2 (19 HP, Rapier), Hector (Wolf Beil ~10 uses), Marcus (Paladin, nearly out of weapons: steel lance ~9, steel sword 1 — trade/buy him a lance), Lowen, Oswin (javelin ~6 + iron lance), Dorcas, Bartre, Rebecca, Serra (Heal), Matthew, **Erk** (new, mage, Thunder — strong vs knights/armour). Battle animations are OFF. Funds 9700 G.

- (s24, attempt 1, notes mid-play turn 5) Prep: no shop in prep (Trade menu has Sell only); gave Matthew's iron sword to Marcus, Bartre's hand axe to Hector, benched Rebecca for Serra. Map ~24x17. Main army starts top-left; **Lyn, Kent, Sain, Wil arrive at the bottom-right next to an ARMORY (lances: steel lance 480, javelin 400), a VENDOR (vulnerary, door key, heal, fire) and a house**; Florina joins next to the main army. **Lyn is a lord here (game over if she dies)** — she dropped to 9 HP by t3 from a myrmidon; Sain Rescued her and carried her to the SE corner. Castle with the boss on the gate is top-right. Enemies (Laus generics: cavaliers w/ iron lance 22 HP, myrmidons 16-21 HP, bandits 22 HP, fighters, thief, archers on the cliff top-centre, a mage, brigands sitting on the mountain top-centre) come at the main army in waves t2-5; a corner pocket (squishies at (0,0)/(1,0)/(1,1), tanks around) + Marcus Horseslayer / Hector axe on the cavaliers worked: 0 losses, 18 enemies left at t5. Houses near the start and the SE are hint-only.

- (s28, attempt 1 continued from turn 9 — s24 hit a usage limit there; s25-27 died instantly) **Boss Bauker** (Knight Lv18, 31 HP, Javelin Atk 19, range 1-2) on the castle gate, far top-right. No mage in the party (Erk not fielded), so plan: Eliwood's **Rapier** and Lyn's **Mani Katti** are both effective vs armour — use them, then pull Eliwood out of javelin range (rescue/canto) because Bauker hits him for ~14. **Reinforcement cavaliers spawn on the TOP EDGE at the start-area columns (~(1,0)/(3,0)) every turn** — they appear at the end of enemy phase and do not act until the next one; parking units on those two tiles stopped the spawns for a turn. The start area is walled off to the east by a cliff; the only way out is SOUTH-EAST through the gap at roughly x=5-7, y=7-9 (where Hector/Marcus are), then east along row ~8, then north up the yellow road to the castle. Two guard cavaliers sit by the ruined forts north-centre and a red mage + archers near the castle. Armory (SE, Wil's tile) also sells Slim lance, Iron lance, Iron bow, **Steel bow** (bought one for Wil).
- **WON attempt 1 (s28, seized turn 19, no deaths).** Correction to the plan above: the SE region (Lyn/Kent/Sain/Wil) is cut off from the castle by a long cliff running from the forts south-east to the right map edge — Lyn could NOT get there, so Mani Katti was never used. What worked: the cavalier spawns stopped after ~t13 (only 3 enemies left by t15); Marcus + Hector + Eliwood walked east to the twin ruined forts (north-centre), then east along open plain to the castle. **Bauker kill:** Marcus with the **Steel lance** from the tile directly below the gate did ~14 x2 at 83% (31 -> 3; the sword would have done ~8), Hector's **Hand axe** from 2 tiles away (diagonal) finished him. Bauker never moved off the gate. Attacking does NOT give Marcus canto, so he blocked the gate's only entry tile until the next turn — plan the order so the lord can walk in. Eliwood seized t19. Ending: Start -> Save screen (slot 1) -> world map / cutscenes (Start) -> Preparations for the next chapter (a Merlinus dialogue plays on the prep screen; advance it with A, NOT Start). The title card was skipped by Start, so I have no screenshot of it.
- Items/state after Ch16: Marcus's steel lance is now broken/used up (iron sword 28, Horseslayer 10, steel sword 1 left — buy him a lance); Hector's hand axe ~14, Wolf Beil 6; Lyn has 1 Vulnerary, Wil has Steel bow + Vulnerary(2). Funds ~7300 G. Eliwood Lv3-4 (20 HP), Hector Lv6+.

### Chapter 17 — Whereabouts Unknown

**Agent notes:**

- **WON attempt 1 (s29, seized turn 17). Bartre DIED (turn 13 enemy phase, rear guard vs cavalier swarm).** Merlinus's tent was destroyed turn 9-10 by the entrance cavaliers (no lasting penalty).
- **Boss Bernard** (General Lv1, 29 HP, Def 13 +2 throne, Res 10, steel lance Atk 24 + hand axe, Spd 3) sits on the throne (top-right) and **never moved** — his real threat is only the tiles within 2 of the throne. Kill that worked: Marcus steel lance from the tile directly BELOW the throne (13 x2, 87%; boss hits him 13 at 62%), then Hector **Wolf Beil** from the tile LEFT of the throne (forecast 16 dmg, 78% = kill). Eliwood waited 3 tiles away and seized next turn (allies on the adjacent tiles can be walked through).
- **ENDLESS REINFORCEMENTS:** lance/sword **cavaliers** (Lv5, 23 HP, Atk 14) spawn at the bottom-left outside the castle from about turn 7 and keep coming (I saw 6 at once by turn 13). They follow the army up the stairs and along corridor B. A 2-unit wall across the 2-row corridor (Oswin + an axe user, with Erk thundering from behind at range 2 and Serra healing) held them, but Bartre died when he was left on the wall alone. Better plan: **rush the throne** with Marcus/Hector/Kent/Lowen + Eliwood and leave only Oswin + Dorcas + Serra + Erk as the rear guard, walled at a 2-wide corridor.
- **Archer room** (6 archers) sits between corridor C and the top corridor; its door seems to stay closed, so they only shoot over the walls at range 2. Walk the TOP row of the top corridor (3 tiles from their room) and stay out of tiles directly above/below the room interior.
- Route that worked: stairs -> hall A -> west along corridor B -> west column (x=0-1) north -> top corridor east (top row) -> throne room (top-right; the knight guards come out to whoever is close; Marcus' lance counters kill them).
- (s29, attempt 1, notes mid-play turn 6) Prep: swapped Rebecca->Erk and Matthew->Kent; via Prep Trade gave Sain's 2 Steel lances to Marcus and Kent (+Sain's Javelin to Kent) — Marcus had no lance. Battle start: Merlinus asks "Deploy Merlinus?" (chose Yes, tent sits at the start, right of the stairs). Map = indoor castle, 17 wide x ~28 tall, start at the BOTTOM centre on grass below a 3-wide staircase (the only way in). Enemies: Laus archers (21 HP, Atk 12, iron/short bow — no melee counter), knights (19 HP, Def 10, Res 1, iron lance Atk 13), a Flux shaman (17 HP) wandering the SW, Raven (enemy Mercenary Lv5, 25 HP, steel sword Atk 16 — breaks out of the middle cell turn 2; recruit needs Priscilla, not in party), green NPC Caelin soldiers + Lucius in the cell at the right. Most enemies stay put until approached. Marcus (steel lance, 27 atk, x2) one-rounds archers/knights and takes ~1 dmg — he's the spearhead. Layout (bottom->top): stairs -> hall A (wide) -> corridor B (full width, closed on the right) -> WEST column (x=0-2) has stairs up to corridor C -> 3 cells -> top corridor -> throne top-RIGHT with knights flanking + boss (armoured, shield).
- (s28 handover, before play) The game loaded **Preparations, header "Chapter 16"** (Eliwood-story numbering), objective **"Seize throne"** — this is the Hector-numbered Ch17 "Whereabouts Unknown" heading. **Merlinus** (merchant / convoy) introduced himself on the prep screen. Saved to slot 1 after Ch15/16 (slot shows "Ch. 15: Noble Lady of Caelin"). Pick list is 10/10 (default: Eliwood, Marcus, Lowen, Bartre, Hector, Oswin, Dorcas, Serra, Rebecca, Matthew; Lyn and Sain greyed/not picked) — I did not change it. Consider fielding Erk if the throne boss is armoured, and Lyn (Mani Katti is effective vs armour/cavalry).

### Chapter 18 — Pirate Ship

**Agent notes:**

- (s29 handover, before play) Title card **"Ch. 17: Pirate Ship"** (no 17x gaiden offered). Saved to slot 1 after Ch16/17 (slot shows "Ch. 16: Whereabouts Unknown"). Game left on the **Preparations** screen, header "Chapter 17", objective **"Survive"**. Opening scene: on a ship deck with an old sailor (Fargus-like captain). **Bartre is dead.** Team state: Marcus (Paladin, steel lance ~10 uses left, Horseslayer 10, steel sword 1, Door key, Mine; an Iron sword went to Merlinus's convoy) is still the carry; Hector's Wolf Beil and Hand axe are both nearly broken (~4 uses each) — get him a new axe if any shop/convoy has one; Kent has steel lance/javelin/iron sword; Erk (Thunder) is excellent vs knights; Oswin is the wall. Prep-trade spare weapons from benched Sain (iron lance) / Lyn / Wil if needed.

- (s30, attempt 1, turn 1) Objective **"Survive for 11 turns or defeat leader"**, 20 enemies (Black Fang mercenaries Lv6 22 HP etc.). Prep: benched Lowen for Erk; prep-trade gave Sain's Iron lance(45) + Lowen's Javelin to Marcus, Lowen's Hammer to Hector. Declined Merlinus. Party starts on the raised FORECASTLE at the top of the middle ship (rows 2-3 of the view); it is reachable only by TWO stair tiles (left stair and right stair below the railing; the tiles beside them are "Fence"). Plan: hold the two stair tops with tanks. A **shop** door is on the middle deck (bottom-left, below the barrel).

- (s34, attempt 1 continued from turn 3 — s30 played t1-3, s31-33 died instantly) **Erk DIED enemy phase 4**: I left him on the forecastle's front row (row 3, the row just above the railing) after he attacked; shamans (Flux range 1-2, Atk 12) walked onto the lower-deck tile 2 below him and killed him. Enemy wave = Black Fang **shamans** (20 HP, Def 3, Res 5 — physical units kill them easily, Oswin 18x2, Dorcas steel axe 20 = one-shot) + mercenaries (one has a Lancereaver; Marcus uses the **Longsword** vs mercs) + an archer. **Geometry (when the camera shows the forecastle at the top):** left stair = Stairs tile directly below the left gap in the railing, its top tile is the gap itself (Deck); our blocker stands one tile ABOVE the gap (Oswin). Right stair top is the gap in the right railing; better blocker spot is the tile ABOVE the gap too (Dorcas) — then only 2 tiles can hit the blocker (the gap tile + the stair tile, range 2). Every other front-row tile is within range 2 of the lower deck: keep everyone but the 2 blockers in the back rows. Serra heals the left blocker from the tile behind him. Using an item gives cavalry Canto (A on own tile -> Wait).
- **WON attempt 1 (s34, survived 11 turns; Erk died t4).** Routine that worked t6-t11: each turn the left blocker (Oswin, iron lance 18 dmg, 98% hit) kills or chips whatever stands on the left gap, Serra (tile behind him) heals him, and on the right Marcus/Kent **javelin the gap from 2 tiles back** (no counter) or Marcus blocks the tile above the gap with the javelin equipped (counters shamans at range 2). Mercenaries do 0-1 to Oswin/Marcus; only the shamans hurt. When a blocker drops below ~half, rotate: pull him back next to Eliwood, take a vulnerary by Trade, drink it, and put a fresh unit in. Enemy reinforcements arrive from the south on t7 and t10. **Turn 10-11: an enemy pegasus knight flies in over the sea** — on the last turn Hector **Rescued** Serra and Dorcas Rescued Eliwood so nobody fragile could be hit; Marcus killed the pegasus on the counter. The chapter ends after enemy phase 11 (Fargus: "Ahoy! I'm back!"), then the Save screen (slot 1), then the title card.

### Chapter 19 — The Dread Isle

**Agent notes:**

- (s34 handover, before play) Title card **"Ch. 18: The Dread Isle"**. Saved to slot 1 after Pirate Ship (slot shows "Ch. 17: Pirate Ship"). Game left on the **Preparations** screen (cursor on Pick Units), header "Chapter 18", objective **"Defeat Uhai"**. A short cutscene before prep showed Eliwood with a teal-haired girl (Ninian) and a "Dragon's Gate" caption. **Dead: Bartre, Erk** (no mage left in the party — Lucius / Serra? check the pick list for a magic user). Team state: Marcus (Paladin, Longsword ~14, Iron lance 40, Steel lance 10, Javelin ~8) is the carry; Oswin Lv12ish (iron lance only) is the wall; Kent (javelin/steel lance/iron sword) 18/28 at the end; Dorcas (steel axe ~10 uses); Hector (Wolf Beil ~4, Hand axe ~5, Hammer 20); Eliwood holds Rapier + Marcus's old **Horseslayer** (useless to him — trade it back to Marcus/Kent); Serra Heal ~6 uses + Vulnerary. All vulneraries except Serra's are used up. Uhai is a Black Fang **Nomad Trooper** (bow + sword, cavalry) in the real game — Horseslayer/Longsword/Rapier are effective against him.

- **Attempt 1 LOST (s35, game over enemy phase 5: LYN died; Kent died enemy phase 4).** **Lyn is a lord here: if she dies it is GAME OVER.** Prep (attempt 1): fielded the default 12 (Eliwood, Marcus, Hector, Oswin, Dorcas, Serra, Kent, Lowen, Rebecca, Matthew, Lyn, Sain); benched Wil + Florina; gave Eliwood's Horseslayer to Marcus (Marcus: Longsword, Iron lance, Steel lance, Horseslayer; Eliwood got Marcus's Vulnerary). Declined Merlinus. **Dart** (pirate, 34 HP, iron axe, walks on water) joins automatically at the start.
- **Fog of war.** Start = peninsula top-left: sea to the NORTH and WEST, a river to the SOUTH crossed by a **2-wide bridge** (about 4-6 tiles south of the start group, slightly left), and a river to the EAST with bridges further east. Enemies come from EVERY side: (a) turns 1-4 a south wave of **Lv5 cavaliers (23 HP, iron lance Atk 14)** and **nomads (horse archers, 20-21 HP, iron bow / LONGBOW range 2-3, NO melee counter)** crosses the south bridge; (b) **pirates (22 HP, iron axe Atk 15, they walk on sea/river)** come out of the NORTH sea onto the start area on turns 2-3 (one hit Lyn 26->5 in one enemy phase!), one from the WEST coast turn 1, and more through the EAST river; (c) a green NPC **Fiora** (pegasus knight) arrives turn 3 in the middle of the start area — Eliwood has NO Talk option with her (probably Florina recruits her); she died to a pirate on enemy phase 5.
- **Sain is useless here**: his only weapon is a Steel sword he cannot wield (greyed). Lowen has only an Iron sword (11 uses). Bench Sain (and consider benching Lyn to remove a game-over condition — she is not required; Wil with Steel bow / Iron bow is a better pick).
- **Bridge hold that worked t1-3:** two blockers on the two tiles at the north end of the bridge (only those 2 tiles touch it) kill the cavaliers on counters; Marcus's **Longsword** does 21 x2 at 100% to cavaliers/nomads. But Kent (28 HP) was left on the right blocker tile at 12 HP and died. **Rotate the blockers when they drop under ~60%**, and bring Oswin (slow, 3 turns from the start) down to the bridge as the permanent second blocker.
- Mistakes that lost it: (1) Lyn left on the north edge turn 2 (pirates from the sea); (2) Lyn used to finish a pirate at the river bend t4 and left there at 21 HP — enemy phase 5 several enemies (cavalier + pirates/nomads) converged on her. **Never end a turn with a lord on the outer ring.** Keep Eliwood/Lyn/Hector inside a ring of units.
- (s35, attempt 2, notes mid-play turn 4) Prep: benched Lyn + Sain, fielded Wil + Florina; Lyn's Vulnerary -> Lowen, Marcus's Steel lance -> Lowen (via Eliwood), Eliwood's Horseslayer -> Marcus. **Florina CAN Talk to Fiora** (Fiora arrives t3 as a green NPC next to the start group): Fiora joins = Lv7 pegasus, 21 HP, Javelin + **Axereaver** (one-shots damaged pirates, 100% hit) + Vulnerary. **Rebecca died enemy phase 3** on the tile just north-east of the bridge mouth: the river bank EAST of the bridge is land — nomads/cavaliers come along the east river bend to that tile, so that "pocket" is NOT sealed; only park tanks there. Serra's Heal staff has only 2 uses left at t4 (she has 2 Vulneraries). Pirates keep arriving from the north/west sea (about one per turn t1-4) — keep Oswin/Dorcas/Wil on the north side to kill them; Oswin takes 0 from pirates.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 9) Holding the start area worked: by turn 9 the waves (pirates from the north/west sea every turn t1-8, cavaliers + Short/Long-bow nomads from the south bridge and the east river bend t1-8) were all dead, no further losses after Rebecca. Eliwood was kept safe by being Rescued (Florina, then Give to Oswin). Minimap (Start): the map is ~25 wide x ~34 tall; start top-left; Uhai must be far SOUTH (big forest, mountains bottom-left). Lowen + Marcus stand on the forts at the south end of the start bridge.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 13) South of the start bridge = thick forest, mountains SW, thickets SE (slow). EAST of the start bridge the land continues past the pink "snag" tiles (passable, not a wall) to a river loop with bridges (one at the loop's west side ~5 tiles east of the start bridge). A monk (Lightning, weak) came from there t12; lone cavaliers trickle in from the south. Kent dropped to 1 HP from enemy-phase hits — check HP every turn before attacking.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 18) **The whole SOUTH half is empty forest/thicket (wasted turns 10-17 scouting it): map bottom is ~10 rows below the start bridge; mountains SW.** Only stray monks/myrmidon/nomads wander there. The minimap shows a brown building in the far TOP-RIGHT corner and enemies kept arriving from the EAST bridges near the top — **Uhai is almost certainly in the NE corner, across the eastern river** (route: from the start area go EAST along the north, cross the bridge east of the start bridge's river loop near the top). Go there directly next attempt. **Correction t23: Marcus reached the NE corner and the small top piece of the middle island — EMPTY too.** Not yet scouted: the interior of the river loop in the centre (south of the river X-junction) and the bottom-centre. Dart carries a **Torch** (use it to light the fog).

## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

- No tutorial prompts appear; free play. Lyn: 16 HP, Iron sword, 2 Vulneraries. Map: Lyn starts bottom-right; one Bandit (20 HP, iron axe, 10 dmg / ~39% hit) mid-left; Batta (Brigand, 21 HP, Str5 Def3, iron axe, does 10 dmg to Lyn at 40% hit) stands on the gate top-left and NEVER moves (Batta does not leave the gate).
- Bandit walks toward Lyn; Lyn doubles it and killed it in one round from turn 2.
- **Attempt 1 LOST:** Lyn attacked Batta at 16/16 HP. He hit her in combat (16→6) and again on his enemy phase → dead. Lesson: attacking on your own phase exposes Lyn to TWO swings (his counter + his own phase) before she can heal.
- **Attempt 2 WON (s01, turn 10, no damage taken):** Lyn waited on her starting forest tile (turns 1-3) and let the bandit come to her; killed it on turn 4. Walked to Batta, then moved to the tile directly south of the gate and chose **Wait** (not Attack): only one swing per turn, Lyn counters x2 for 5 each. Gate heals Batta +2/turn. After two waits he was at 3 HP; then Attack killed him with the first hit. Seize the gate. Lyn hit Lv2.
- General lesson: the forecast's "x2" icon hides Lyn's Mt number; the in-battle HUD shows DMG. Against a stationary boss, "stand adjacent and Wait" = one enemy swing per turn, and you can step away to heal any time.

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. However, your attacks will be unimpeded, giving you a distinct advantage. The same is true for foes. If an enemy is in the woods, he is more difficult to hit. Factoring in your terrain benefits and the weapon triangle is vital in combat. The window at the bottom of the screen gives information on the terrain the cursor is placed on. Check to see what terrain type is advantageous by using the cursor. Now, let’s put this to the test. Select Kent.
4. To give away an item, use the trade command. Trade can only be used by units that are adjacent to one another. Let’s use the trade command now. Select Sain and move him next to Lyn.
5. Now select the trade command. Sain’s and Lyn’s possessions will be displayed together. Use the cursor to select a vulnerary from Lyn’s items, and give it to Sain. After you’ve finished your trade, press the B Button to end the process. The B Button is the cancel button. It can be used to rescind mistaken commands and other things.
6. Place the cursor on Lyn’s items. Press right on the + Control Pad.
7. Press up or down on the + Control Pad, and select a vulnerary. Then, press the A Button.  
   (Lyn’s Vulnerary is selected, the message is repeated if a button other than A or Start is pressed)
8. Press the A Button to accept the vulnerary from Lyn.
9. Press the B Button to stop trading.
10. Sain can now use Lyn’s vulnerary. Select the vulnerary from the items and use it.
11. Furthermore, mounted units have the unique ability to move again. Essentially, this allows cavalry to move the number of spaces left in their movement range if they haven’t done so already. However, the attack command, among others, nullifies the move again ability, so be careful. Select Sain and order him to move again.
12. Mission goals change from chapter to chapter. This chapter’s goal is to defeat all enemies. Check the chapter goals in the window to the upper right of the screen. To open the map menu, place the cursor on an unoccupied space and press the A Button. You can confirm the chapter goals here by choosing Status from the menu. The map menu also has the Suspend command. This is useful if you need to stop a chapter midway. Time to continue this chapter! Best of luck!

**Agent notes:**

- (s29 handover, before play) Title card **"Ch. 17: Pirate Ship"** (no 17x gaiden offered). Saved to slot 1 after Ch16/17 (slot shows "Ch. 16: Whereabouts Unknown"). Game left on the **Preparations** screen, header "Chapter 17", objective **"Survive"**. Opening scene: on a ship deck with an old sailor (Fargus-like captain). **Bartre is dead.** Team state: Marcus (Paladin, steel lance ~10 uses left, Horseslayer 10, steel sword 1, Door key, Mine; an Iron sword went to Merlinus's convoy) is still the carry; Hector's Wolf Beil and Hand axe are both nearly broken (~4 uses each) — get him a new axe if any shop/convoy has one; Kent has steel lance/javelin/iron sword; Erk (Thunder) is excellent vs knights; Oswin is the wall. Prep-trade spare weapons from benched Sain (iron lance) / Lyn / Wil if needed.

- (s30, attempt 1, turn 1) Objective **"Survive for 11 turns or defeat leader"**, 20 enemies (Black Fang mercenaries Lv6 22 HP etc.). Prep: benched Lowen for Erk; prep-trade gave Sain's Iron lance(45) + Lowen's Javelin to Marcus, Lowen's Hammer to Hector. Declined Merlinus. Party starts on the raised FORECASTLE at the top of the middle ship (rows 2-3 of the view); it is reachable only by TWO stair tiles (left stair and right stair below the railing; the tiles beside them are "Fence"). Plan: hold the two stair tops with tanks. A **shop** door is on the middle deck (bottom-left, below the barrel).

- (s34, attempt 1 continued from turn 3 — s30 played t1-3, s31-33 died instantly) **Erk DIED enemy phase 4**: I left him on the forecastle's front row (row 3, the row just above the railing) after he attacked; shamans (Flux range 1-2, Atk 12) walked onto the lower-deck tile 2 below him and killed him. Enemy wave = Black Fang **shamans** (20 HP, Def 3, Res 5 — physical units kill them easily, Oswin 18x2, Dorcas steel axe 20 = one-shot) + mercenaries (one has a Lancereaver; Marcus uses the **Longsword** vs mercs) + an archer. **Geometry (when the camera shows the forecastle at the top):** left stair = Stairs tile directly below the left gap in the railing, its top tile is the gap itself (Deck); our blocker stands one tile ABOVE the gap (Oswin). Right stair top is the gap in the right railing; better blocker spot is the tile ABOVE the gap too (Dorcas) — then only 2 tiles can hit the blocker (the gap tile + the stair tile, range 2). Every other front-row tile is within range 2 of the lower deck: keep everyone but the 2 blockers in the back rows. Serra heals the left blocker from the tile behind him. Using an item gives cavalry Canto (A on own tile -> Wait).
- **WON attempt 1 (s34, survived 11 turns; Erk died t4).** Routine that worked t6-t11: each turn the left blocker (Oswin, iron lance 18 dmg, 98% hit) kills or chips whatever stands on the left gap, Serra (tile behind him) heals him, and on the right Marcus/Kent **javelin the gap from 2 tiles back** (no counter) or Marcus blocks the tile above the gap with the javelin equipped (counters shamans at range 2). Mercenaries do 0-1 to Oswin/Marcus; only the shamans hurt. When a blocker drops below ~half, rotate: pull him back next to Eliwood, take a vulnerary by Trade, drink it, and put a fresh unit in. Enemy reinforcements arrive from the south on t7 and t10. **Turn 10-11: an enemy pegasus knight flies in over the sea** — on the last turn Hector **Rescued** Serra and Dorcas Rescued Eliwood so nobody fragile could be hit; Marcus killed the pegasus on the counter. The chapter ends after enemy phase 11 (Fargus: "Ahoy! I'm back!"), then the Save screen (slot 1), then the title card.

**Agent notes:**

All vulneraries except Serra's are used up. Uhai is a Black Fang **Nomad Trooper** (bow + sword, cavalry) in the real game — Horseslayer/Longsword/Rapier are effective against him.

- **Attempt 1 LOST (s35, game over enemy phase 5: LYN died; Kent died enemy phase 4).** **Lyn is a lord here: if she dies it is GAME OVER.** Prep (attempt 1): fielded the default 12 (Eliwood, Marcus, Hector, Oswin, Dorcas, Serra, Kent, Lowen, Rebecca, Matthew, Lyn, Sain); benched Wil + Florina; gave Eliwood's Horseslayer to Marcus (Marcus: Longsword, Iron lance, Steel lance, Horseslayer; Eliwood got Marcus's Vulnerary). - **Fog of war.** Start = peninsula top-left: sea to the NORTH and WEST, a river to the SOUTH crossed by a **2-wide bridge** (about 4-6 tiles south of the start group, slightly left), and a river to the EAST with bridges further east. - **Bridge hold that worked t1-3:** two blockers on the two tiles at the north end of the bridge (only those 2 tiles touch it) kill the cavaliers on counters; Marcus's **Longsword** does 21 x2 at 100% to cavaliers/nomads. But Kent (28 HP) was left on the right blocker tile at 12 HP and died. **Rotate the blockers when they drop under ~60%**, and bring Oswin (slow, 3 turns from the start) down to the bridge as the permanent second blocker.
- Mistakes that lost it: (1) Lyn left on the north edge turn 2 (pirates from the sea); (2) Lyn used to finish a pirate at the river bend t4 and left there at 21 HP — enemy phase 5 several enemies (cavalier + pirates/nomads) converged on her. **Never end a turn with a lord on the outer ring.** Keep Eliwood/Lyn/Hector inside a ring of units.
- (s35, attempt 2, notes mid-play turn 4) Prep: benched Lyn + Sain, fielded Wil + Florina; Lyn's Vulnerary -> Lowen, Marcus's Steel lance -> Lowen (via Eliwood), Eliwood's Horseslayer -> Marcus. **Florina CAN Talk to Fiora** (Fiora arrives t3 as a green NPC next to the start group): Fiora joins = Lv7 pegasus, 21 HP, Javelin + **Axereaver** (one-shots damaged pirates, 100% hit) + Vulnerary. **Rebecca died enemy phase 3** on the tile just north-east of the bridge mouth: the river bank EAST of the bridge is land — nomads/cavaliers come along the east river bend to that tile, so that "pocket" is NOT sealed; only park tanks there. Serra's Heal staff has only 2 uses left at t4 (she has 2 Vulneraries). Pirates keep arriving from the north/west sea (about one per turn t1-4) — keep Oswin/Dorcas/Wil on the north side to kill them; Oswin takes 0 from pirates.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 9) Holding the start area worked: by turn 9 the waves (pirates from the north/west sea every turn t1-8, cavaliers + Short/Long-bow nomads from the south bridge and the east river bend t1-8) were all dead, no further losses after Rebecca. Eliwood was kept safe by being Rescued (Florina, then Give to Oswin). Minimap (Start): the map is ~25 wide x ~34 tall; start top-left; Uhai must be far SOUTH (big forest, mountains bottom-left). Lowen + Marcus stand on the forts at the south end of the start bridge.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 13) South of the start bridge = thick forest, mountains SW, thickets SE (slow). EAST of the start bridge the land continues past the pink "snag" tiles (passable, not a wall) to a river loop with bridges (one at the loop's west side ~5 tiles east of the start bridge). A monk (Lightning, weak) came from there t12; lone cavaliers trickle in from the south. Kent dropped to 1 HP from enemy-phase hits — check HP every turn before attacking.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 18) **The whole SOUTH half is empty forest/thicket (wasted turns 10-17 scouting it): map bottom is ~10 rows below the start bridge; mountains SW.** Only stray monks/myrmidon/nomads wander there. The minimap shows a brown building in the far TOP-RIGHT corner and enemies kept arriving from the EAST bridges near the top — **Uhai is almost certainly in the NE corner, across the eastern river** (route: from the start area go EAST along the north, cross the bridge east of the start bridge's river loop near the top). ## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

- No tutorial prompts appear; free play. Lyn: 16 HP, Iron sword, 2 Vulneraries. Map: Lyn starts bottom-right; one Bandit (20 HP, iron axe, 10 dmg / ~39% hit) mid-left; Batta (Brigand, 21 HP, Str5 Def3, iron axe, does 10 dmg to Lyn at 40% hit) stands on the gate top-left and NEVER moves (Batta does not leave the gate).
- Bandit walks toward Lyn; Lyn doubles it and killed it in one round from turn 2.
- **Attempt 1 LOST:** Lyn attacked Batta at 16/16 HP. He hit her in combat (16→6) and again on his enemy phase → dead. Lesson: attacking on your own phase exposes Lyn to TWO swings (his counter + his own phase) before she can heal.
- **Attempt 2 WON (s01, turn 10, no damage taken):** Lyn waited on her starting forest tile (turns 1-3) and let the bandit come to her; killed it on turn 4. Walked to Batta, then moved to the tile directly south of the gate and chose **Wait** (not Attack): only one swing per turn, Lyn counters x2 for 5 each. Gate heals Batta +2/turn. After two waits he was at 3 HP; then Attack killed him with the first hit. Seize the gate. Lyn hit Lv2.
- General lesson: the forecast's "x2" icon hides Lyn's Mt number; the in-battle HUD shows DMG. Against a stationary boss, "stand adjacent and Wait" = one enemy swing per turn, and you can step away to heal any time.

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. ## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.
2. “You have selected Lyn. When a unit is selected, the map changes color like so. Lyn can move anywhere in the blue area. Move her to the space with the flashing cursor. Place your cursor there, and then press the A Button to finish.”
3. “Select Lyn.”
4. “Move to one of the areas adjacent to the bandit.”
5. Press the A Button after placing the cursor next to the enemy.
6. “Select attack!”
7. “Select Lyn.”
8. Move to the space marked by the flashing cursor.
9. Open the Item menu and select a vulnerary. Next, choose Use.
10. Lyn gains experience in each encounter. When she has enough experience, she will level up. As she increases in level, her abilities improve. Over time, she will grow much stronger. It’s time to bring this chapter to a close. Select Lyn and move her to the gate where Batta the Beast was standing. Select Seize to complete Lyn’s victory and your own!
11. Travel with Lyn, Mark. Give her your aid, and master the art of combat. Complete the tasks set out in each chapter, and help Lyn in her quest. Turn the instruction window on or off by pressing SELECT.

**Agent notes:**

- No tutorial prompts appear; free play. Lyn: 16 HP, Iron sword, 2 Vulneraries. Map: Lyn starts bottom-right; one Bandit (20 HP, iron axe, 10 dmg / ~39% hit) mid-left; Batta (Brigand, 21 HP, Str5 Def3, iron axe, does 10 dmg to Lyn at 40% hit) stands on the gate top-left and NEVER moves (Batta does not leave the gate).
- Bandit walks toward Lyn; Lyn doubles it and killed it in one round from turn 2.
- **Attempt 1 LOST:** Lyn attacked Batta at 16/16 HP. He hit her in combat (16→6) and again on his enemy phase → dead. Lesson: attacking on your own phase exposes Lyn to TWO swings (his counter + his own phase) before she can heal.
- **Attempt 2 WON (s01, turn 10, no damage taken):** Lyn waited on her starting forest tile (turns 1-3) and let the bandit come to her; killed it on turn 4. Walked to Batta, then moved to the tile directly south of the gate and chose **Wait** (not Attack): only one swing per turn, Lyn counters x2 for 5 each. Gate heals Batta +2/turn. After two waits he was at 3 HP; then Attack killed him with the first hit. Seize the gate. Lyn hit Lv2.
- General lesson: the forecast's "x2" icon hides Lyn's Mt number; the in-battle HUD shows DMG. Against a stationary boss, "stand adjacent and Wait" = one enemy swing per turn, and you can step away to heal any time.

### Chapter 1 — Footsteps of Fate

**Tutorial:**

1. Blue units are allies. Direct them on the field as you did with Lyn before. Be warned: if Lyn is defeated, your journey is over, as is your game. If other blue units are beaten, the game will continue, but fallen companions will be unable to return to battle for the rest of the tutorial. Use caution and good judgment. After all blue units have been moved, it automatically becomes the enemy’s turn. To begin with, select Sain. Place the cursor on Sain, and press the A Button.
2. Weapons possess a unique hierarchy. Swords best axes. Axes best lances. Lances best swords. This is called the weapon triangle. Remembering this is of the utmost importance. First, let’s illustrate that swords are strong against axes. Select Kent.
3. Each type of terrain has unique characteristics. For example, look at woods and plains. Battle an enemy from the woods, and the enemy will likely miss you. ## Chapters

### Prologue — A Girl from the Plains

**Tutorial:**

1. Unit Information: Lyn is the blue unit. The enemy units are red. Mark, you are green. Essentially, battle consists of blue (allied) units and red (enemy) units taking turns moving on the field. You’re only here as a strategist, Mark. You will only appear during special events. Your job as strategist is to place the cursor on blue units to issue their orders. First, select a unit. Place the cursor on Lyn and press the A Button.

Bauker never moved off the gate. Attacking does NOT give Marcus canto, so he blocked the gate's only entry tile until the next turn — plan the order so the lord can walk in. Eliwood seized t19. Ending: Start -> Save screen (slot 1) -> world map / cutscenes (Start) -> Preparations for the next chapter (a Merlinus dialogue plays on the prep screen; advance it with A, NOT Start). The title card was skipped by Start, so I have no screenshot of it.

**Agent notes:**

All vulneraries except Serra's are used up. Uhai is a Black Fang **Nomad Trooper** (bow + sword, cavalry) in the real game — Horseslayer/Longsword/Rapier are effective against him.

- **Attempt 1 LOST (s35, game over enemy phase 5: LYN died; Kent died enemy phase 4).** **Lyn is a lord here: if she dies it is GAME OVER.** Prep (attempt 1): fielded the default 12 (Eliwood, Marcus, Hector, Oswin, Dorcas, Serra, Kent, Lowen, Rebecca, Matthew, Lyn, Sain); benched Wil + Florina; gave Eliwood's Horseslayer to Marcus (Marcus: Longsword, Iron lance, Steel lance, Horseslayer; Eliwood got Marcus's Vulnerary). - (s35, attempt 2, notes mid-play turn 4) Prep: benched Lyn + Sain, fielded Wil + Florina; Lyn's Vulnerary -> Lowen, Marcus's Steel lance -> Lowen (via Eliwood), Eliwood's Horseslayer -> Marcus. **Florina CAN Talk to Fiora** (Fiora arrives t3 as a green NPC next to the start group): Fiora joins = Lv7 pegasus, 21 HP, Javelin + **Axereaver** (one-shots damaged pirates, 100% hit) + Vulnerary. **Rebecca died enemy phase 3** on the tile just north-east of the bridge mouth: the river bank EAST of the bridge is land — nomads/cavaliers come along the east river bend to that tile, so that "pocket" is NOT sealed; only park tanks there. Serra's Heal staff has only 2 uses left at t4 (she has 2 Vulneraries). Pirates keep arriving from the north/west sea (about one per turn t1-4) — keep Oswin/Dorcas/Wil on the north side to kill them; Oswin takes 0 from pirates.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 9) Holding the start area worked: by turn 9 the waves (pirates from the north/west sea every turn t1-8, cavaliers + Short/Long-bow nomads from the south bridge and the east river bend t1-8) were all dead, no further losses after Rebecca. Eliwood was kept safe by being Rescued (Florina, then Give to Oswin). Minimap (Start): the map is ~25 wide x ~34 tall; start top-left; Uhai must be far SOUTH (big forest, mountains bottom-left). Lowen + Marcus stand on the forts at the south end of the start bridge.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 13) South of the start bridge = thick forest, mountains SW, thickets SE (slow). EAST of the start bridge the land continues past the pink "snag" tiles (passable, not a wall) to a river loop with bridges (one at the loop's west side ~5 tiles east of the start bridge). A monk (Lightning, weak) came from there t12; lone cavaliers trickle in from the south. Kent dropped to 1 HP from enemy-phase hits — check HP every turn before attacking.
- (s35, attempt 2, turn 18) **The whole SOUTH half is empty forest/thicket (wasted turns 10-17 scouting it): map bottom is ~10 rows below the start bridge; mountains SW.** Only stray monks/myrmidon/nomads wander there. The minimap shows a brown building in the far TOP-RIGHT corner and enemies kept arriving from the EAST bridges near the top — **Uhai is almost certainly in the NE corner, across the eastern river** (route: from the start area go EAST along the north, cross the bridge east of the start bridge's river loop near the top). Go there directly next attempt. **Correction t23: Marcus reached the NE corner and the small top piece of the middle island — EMPTY too.** Not yet scouted: the interior of the river loop in the centre (south of the river X-junction) and the bottom-centre. Dart carries a **Torch** (use it to light the fog).
- (s39, attempt 2 continued at TURN 30 — s36-38 left no notes/screens) **Map is SMALL: ~17 wide x 23 tall** (camera stops scrolling right ~2 cols past the start view; the minimap is the whole map). Fog vision is only ~3 tiles. Still no Uhai at t31. Checked empty at t30-31: SE corner (Marcus), bottom-centre (Lowen), SW = peaks only, the river-loop interior (Dart's Torch lit a radius ~5 around map ~(10,13) — empty), the east strip around the bridge east of the loop (Marcus), the NE corner (Fiora). Torch works: Item -> Torch -> Use, lights a big radius immediately after the animation. Unit menu (map menu -> Unit) + A on a name jumps the cursor to that unit — fastest way to find people. Stray lone Black Fang cavaliers (23 HP) still wander the south.
- **FOUND UHAI (s39, t33) — BOTTOM-RIGHT, on the map's BOTTOM ROW, ~6 tiles EAST of the bottom-centre forest (about 4 tiles left of the SE corner), in the forest/thicket strip.** He never moves (stood there 33 turns). Fog hid him because vision is only ~3 and he's tucked in the thicket. Next attempt: go straight there (south over the start bridge, then south-east through the forest), and light it with the Torch. **Uhai stats:** Nomad Trooper Lv7, 33 HP, Str 15 Skl 13 Spd 12 Def 12 Res 13, Mov 8, Avoid 48 in forest. Weapons: Steel sword (range 1, Atk 23, hit 103), **Longbow (range 2-3)**, Short bow, Orion's bolt (drop). He counters at ANY range 1-3 — no safe ranged chip. Bows = effective vs Florina/Fiora: keep fliers 4+ tiles away. Effective weapons vs him (cavalry): Marcus's Horseslayer/Longsword, Eliwood's Rapier.
- **WON attempt 2 (s39, Uhai killed player phase 36; deaths this attempt: Rebecca).** Kill: Marcus with the **Horseslayer (a LANCE: effective vs cavalry AND triangle-beats his steel sword)** stood on the tile directly ABOVE Uhai and Waited (fog hides him, so no Attack option until he is revealed). Enemy phase: Uhai swung the steel sword at Marcus and Marcus's counter took him 33 -> 12. Next turn Marcus attacked: 21 dmg, 84% -> dead. Uhai did 0 to Marcus (both his swings missed; he'd do ~11). Stage Marcus 4 tiles away the turn before (outside the Longbow's 3 range). The whole chapter can be done in ~8 turns if you go straight there.

content.text:
I won Chapter 19 (The Dread Isle) on attempt 2. Rebecca died earlier in this attempt (s35, turn 3); no one else was lost.

- **Starting point:** I picked up mid-attempt at turn 30. Sessions s36–s38 had left no notes or screenshots, and in about 30 turns nobody had found Uhai in the fog.
- **Finding Uhai:** the map is small (about 17 by 23 tiles), but each unit only sees about 3 tiles. Dart passed his Torch to Florina, who flew it around the map. On turn 33 it lit up Uhai standing on the bottom row in the south-east forest. He never moved all chapter.
- **The kill:** Marcus equipped the Horseslayer, a lance that is effective against Uhai and beats his sword, and waited on the tile next to him. During the enemy phase Uhai attacked and missed, and Marcus's counter took him from 33 to 12 HP. On turn 36 Marcus attacked for 21 damage and killed him. Marcus took no damage.
- **Item choice:** Uhai dropped an Orion's Bolt into Marcus's full inventory. I discarded his Lightning tome to make room; it's the item Marcus could most easily lose.
- **Save prompt:** I chose Save to slot 1, the slot already in use.
- **Where it stops:** the title card read "Ch. 19: Dragon's Gate", with no gaiden offered. The game is on the Preparations screen, objective "Seize throne". I didn't press Start.
- **Notes for the next session:** `CURRENT_RUN_STRATEGY.md` now has Uhai's location, stats and the method that worked, so a replay should take about 8 turns. I also added a handover section for the next chapter with the team and inventory state.
- **`run_state.json`:** Rebecca added to `dead`, the chapter recorded as completed in 2 attempts by s39, `current_chapter` set to "Chapter 20 — Dragon's Gate", `attempts` reset to 0. The file still parses as valid JSON.
